| FR-128 | Preference persistence | The chosen preference is persisted and re-applied on the next session, after sign-out/in, reload and app restart. | must-have |
| FR-129 | Immediate application | Changing the preference or the system signal re-themes every already-rendered surface without reload. | must-have |
| FR-130 | No flash of wrong theme | On load the correct theme is applied before first paint, avoiding a flash of the wrong theme. | must-have |
| FR-131 | Cross-screen consistency | Every screen, modal, overlay and empty/loading/error state honours the active theme. | must-have |
| FR-132 | Scheduled auto switching | The user can optionally schedule theme switching by time of day. | nice-to-have |
| FR-133 | Contrast compliance | Text and UI meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast in both themes, per NFR-79. | must-have |
| FR-134 | Semantic colour tokens | Components consume semantic tokens rather than hard-coded colours so theming is uniform. | should-have |
| FR-135 | Charts and data viz | Analytics (F-4) charts and any data visualisation adapt to the active theme. | must-have |
| FR-136 | Third-party embeds | External content that cannot be themed is shown on a compliant surface. | should-have |
| FR-137 | Images and media | Illustrations/media have theme-appropriate variants or an acceptable neutral treatment. | should-have |
| FR-138 | System signal detection | The product reads `prefers-color-scheme` where available and falls back to `light` when unknown. | must-have |
| FR-139 | User override of system | Selecting `light`/`dark` stops following the system until `system` is re-selected. | must-have |
| FR-140 | Settings entry point | Theme preference is settable from a clearly labelled Settings location. | must-have |
| FR-141 | Account-level default | Theme preference may follow the user across devices without overriding a device-local explicit choice. | should-have |
| FR-142 | Print/export | Printed/exported views remain legible regardless of the active theme. | should-have |
| FR-143 | Reduced motion | Theme transitions respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. | should-have |
| FR-144 | Focus indicators | Focus indicators remain visible in both themes. | must-have |
| FR-145 | Loading state theming | Skeletons, spinners and loaders use theme tokens. | should-have |
| FR-146 | Error state theming | Error, warning and success states remain distinguishable in both themes. | must-have |
| FR-147 | Persistence edge cases | Persistence survives sign-out/sign-in, reload and app restart, reinforcing FR-128. | must-have |
| FR-148 | No layout shift | Switching theme does not cause layout shift (CLS). | should-have |
| FR-149 | Preference reset | The user can reset to the default (`system`) preference. | should-have |
| FR-150 | Accessibility announcement | Changing theme is announced to assistive tech without stealing focus. | must-have |

**Coverage check:** FR-1..FR-150 map one-to-one onto features F-1..F-6 with no gaps, no duplicates and no ids outside the assigned ranges.

## Non-Functional Requirements

Product-wide NFRs below apply to every feature (F-1 .. F-6). Ids are global and unique across the spec; feature-scoped NFRs are declared inside their own feature sections and referenced here only by plain text where relevant.

### Performance

| ID | Requirement | Target (measurable) | Measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-1 | Initial load of the app shell on a typical desktop connection | First Contentful Paint ≤ 1.0 s; Time to Interactive ≤ 3.0 s; on a simulated 3G (Fast 3G) profile the interactive shell is usable ≤ 2.0 s | Lab run on throttled profile (e.g. Lighthouse CI) on the production build, median of 5 runs |
| NFR-2 | Largest contentful paint on the primary screens (Today queue, task detail, Progress) | LCP ≤ 2.5 s at p75 | Real-user monitoring (RUM) p75 over trailing 28 days |
| NFR-3 | Visual stability during load and re-theming | Cumulative Layout Shift ≤ 0.1 at p75 | RUM p75 / Lighthouse on production build |
| NFR-4 | Interaction responsiveness | Every user-initiated action (tap, click, key) produces a visible acknowledgement ≤ 100 ms; any operation exceeding 2 s shows a progress/loading indicator | RUM event timing; manual measurement for long operations |
| NFR-5 | Priority scoring and Today-queue recomputation (F-1) | Full recompute for a user with 5,000 active tasks completes ≤ 300 ms; incremental recompute after a single task edit ≤ 50 ms | Server-side timing histogram, p95 |
| NFR-6 | Quick-add capture-to-preview (F-2) | Parse + preview render ≤ 150 ms after the last keystroke, for input up to 280 characters | Client-side timing instrumentation, p95 |
| NFR-7 | Focus-session timer accuracy (F-3) | Displayed session time deviates from wall-clock by ≤ 1 s over a 24-hour continuous session; timer display refreshes at least once per second | Automated timing test comparing monotonic clock to rendered value |
| NFR-8 | Progress analytics rendering (F-4) | Dashboard for a selected period first contentful render ≤ 2 s and fully rendered ≤ 3 s for up to 5 years of a user's data | Server aggregation timing + client render timing, p95 |
| NFR-9 | Integration sync throughput and latency (F-5) | An incremental sync completes ≤ 60 s after trigger for a source with ≤ 10,000 changed items; initial/backfill sync reports progress and does not block the UI | Sync worker timing histogram, p95; UI must remain interactive during backfill |
| NFR-10 | Theme application latency (F-6) | A preference change or OS colour-scheme change re-themes all rendered surfaces within one animation frame (≤ 16 ms) with no flash of the previous theme on next load | Client timing test; visual regression of first paint |
| NFR-11 | Bundle discipline | Initial JS payload for the shell ≤ 200 KB gzipped; feature areas (Focus, Progress, Integrations) are code-split | Build-size budget check in CI (fails build on regression) |

### Scalability & Availability

| ID | Requirement | Target (measurable) | Measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-12 | Per-user data volume | Support ≥ 50,000 active tasks and ≥ 500,000 historical events per user without degradation beyond the NFR-5/NFR-8 budgets | Load test with synthetic user at that volume |
| NFR-13 | Concurrency | Support ≥ 10,000 concurrent active users with p95 API latency ≤ 500 ms for read endpoints and ≤ 800 ms for write endpoints | Load test against staging at target concurrency |
| NFR-14 | Availability | Monthly availability ≥ 99.9 % for core read/write paths (task list, quick add, focus timer persistence) | Uptime monitor over calendar month |
| NFR-15 | Horizontal scalability | Application tier scales horizontally without sticky sessions; adding instances increases throughput linearly (within 10 % of ideal) up to 4× baseline | Scale-out benchmark in staging |
| NFR-16 | Elastic capacity | Autoscaling reacts to sustained load within 5 minutes; no 5xx increase during a 3× traffic spike sustained for 15 minutes | Chaos/load test |
| NFR-17 | Graceful degradation | If a non-core subsystem (F-4 analytics, F-5 integrations, F-6 preference service) is unavailable, the core paths (F-1, F-2, F-3) remain fully functional with an in-context degraded-mode notice; no data loss on recovery | Fault-injection test per subsystem |
| NFR-18 | Offline tolerance for in-progress capture | Quick-add entries and focus-session state created while offline are queued and reconciled on reconnect without duplication or loss | Automated offline/reconnect test |

### Security

| ID | Requirement | Target (measurable) | Measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-19 | Transport security | All client↔server and server↔provider traffic uses TLS 1.2 or higher; HSTS enabled; no plaintext HTTP access to authenticated surfaces | Config audit + external TLS scan |
| NFR-20 | Encryption at rest | All persisted user data (tasks, analytics aggregates, integration metadata, focus history) is encrypted at rest with a managed key; rotating keys supported without downtime | Storage configuration audit |
| NFR-21 | Authentication & session safety | Passwords (if used) stored only as salted, adaptive hashes; sessions expire after a configurable idle period and use secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies (or equivalent token handling); no credentials ever written to client storage in plaintext | Code/security review + automated session tests |
| NFR-22 | Third-party authorization (F-5) | Provider credentials are never entered into product-owned credential fields; OAuth access/refresh tokens are encrypted at rest, never logged, never returned to the client, and are revoked on disconnect | Security review + log-scanning test |
| NFR-23 | Tenant/data isolation | A user can access only their own data; every data access is authorized against the requesting identity; cross-tenant access attempts are denied and audited | Automated isolation test suite (must pass on every release) |
| NFR-24 | Input handling hardening | All user-supplied content (titles, tags, integration payloads, webhook bodies) is validated and safely encoded on output; protections against XSS, CSRF, injection, and SSRF (for webhook bridges) are enforced | SAST/DAST in CI + targeted abuse tests |
| NFR-25 | Rate limiting & abuse protection | Authenticated endpoints enforce per-user rate limits; webhook/inbound endpoints enforce per-source limits and reject unauthenticated or oversize payloads | Load test + configuration audit |
| NFR-26 | Auditability of security-relevant events | Authentication, connection grant/revoke, and data-export/delete events are recorded in an append-only audit log with actor, timestamp, and outcome | Log review + automated audit-event tests |
| NFR-27 | Dependency & vulnerability posture | No known high/critical vulnerabilities in production dependencies; scanning runs on every build and blocks release on new high/critical findings | SCA scan gate in CI |

### Data & Residency

| ID | Requirement | Target (measurable) | Measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-28 | Data residency | Users can be pinned to a declared storage region; all primary data and backups for that user remain in the selected region | Configuration + automated residency assertion test |
| NFR-29 | Data ownership & export | The user can export all their data (tasks, focus history, analytics source data, connection metadata) in a machine-readable format; export completes ≤ 5 minutes for a maximum-volume user | End-to-end export test |
| NFR-30 | Right to erasure | A delete request removes or irreversibly anonymizes all personal data within 30 days, including derived analytics aggregates and cached integration data; the completion is recorded in the audit log | Deletion verification test on staging |
| NFR-31 | Retention defaults | Operational logs retained ≤ 90 days by default; analytics source events retained per user-configurable retention with a documented floor and ceiling; no indefinite retention without an explicit policy | Retention configuration audit |
| NFR-32 | Backup & recovery | Automated backups at least daily with an RPO ≤ 24 h and RTO ≤ 4 h for core data; restore is exercised at least quarterly | Backup/restore drill record |
| NFR-33 | Legal basis & consent | Data collection is limited to what each feature requires; integration scopes are minimized to the declared read/write capability; consent for each connected source is recorded and revocable | Scope review + consent-state test |
| NFR-34 | Derived data transparency | Aggregated/derived metrics (F-4) are recomputable from source events and are removed or recomputed when their source data is deleted or corrected | Recomputation test after source mutation |

### Deployment & Environment

| ID | Requirement | Target (measurable) | Measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-35 | Environment separation | Independent development, staging, and production environments with no shared production data in non-production tiers | Environment inventory audit |
| NFR-36 | Reproducible builds & deployment | Every deploy is produced from a versioned, immutable build artifact; deployment is automated and idempotent | CI pipeline audit |
| NFR-37 | Zero-downtime releases | Core paths remain available during deploys and schema migrations; migrations are backward-compatible and reversible | Deploy rehearsal + availability monitor during release |
| NFR-38 | Configuration & secrets management | Configuration is externalized per environment; secrets are injected at runtime from a managed store and never committed to the repository | Secret-scanning gate in CI |
| NFR-39 | Observability | Structured logs, metrics, and distributed traces cover every request path; dashboards and alerts exist for the NFR-1..NFR-18 budgets, error rate, and availability | Observability coverage review; alert-routing test |
| NFR-40 | Rollback | Any release can be rolled back to the previous known-good version within 15 minutes without data loss | Rollback drill |
| NFR-41 | Client platform support | Supported browsers: current and previous major versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge; responsive layouts for viewports 320 px–2560 px; no horizontal scroll at 320 px | Cross-browser/cross-viewport test matrix |
| NFR-42 | Accessibility conformance | WCAG 2.1 Level AA across all features: text contrast ≥ 4.5:1, UI contrast ≥ 3:1, full keyboard operability, semantic landmarks, screen-reader labels, visible focus (≥ 2 px), no flashing > 3 Hz, skip-to-content, and both light and dark themes independently conformant | Automated a11y scan (zero critical) + manual audit for dark-mode parity |
| NFR-43 | Internationalization readiness | UI strings are externalized; dates, times, numbers, and currency render per user locale; layout supports RTL without truncation | Locale/RTL smoke test |
| NFR-44 | Perceived-quality budget monitoring | Performance and availability budgets (NFR-1..NFR-18) are enforced as release gates; a regression beyond budget blocks promotion to production | CI gate configuration audit |

## User Stories

Stories are grouped by feature. Global ids `US-1 .. US-15` belong to F-1, `US-16 .. US-30` to F-2, `US-31 .. US-45` to F-3, `US-46 .. US-60` to F-4, `US-61 .. US-75` to F-5, and `US-76 .. US-90` to F-6. References to other features' ids are plain text only.

### F-1 — Intelligent Task Prioritization

#### US-1: See my work in priority order
- As a busy professional, I want my active tasks ranked for me automatically, so that I always know what to do next without manually sorting.
- Acceptance Criteria: Every active task has a numeric priority score (FR-1); the "Today" queue is sorted by descending score (FR-2); the order is stable across reloads when inputs are unchanged.

#### US-2: Have multiple factors feed the ranking
- As a user with mixed deadlines, I want ranking to consider due dates, importance, effort, age, and dependencies, so that the order reflects real-world urgency.
- Acceptance Criteria: Each listed factor influences the score (FR-3); changing any single factor on a task can change its rank.

#### US-3: Understand why a task is ranked where it is
- As a skeptical user, I want a plain-language explanation per task, so that I can trust the automatic ordering.
- Acceptance Criteria: Each task exposes an explanation naming the dominant factors (FR-5); the explanation is readable without jargon.

#### US-4: Tune the ranking to my style
- As a user who values deadlines over effort, I want to adjust factor weights, so that ranking matches how I actually work.
- Acceptance Criteria: Weight controls exist per factor (FR-4); saving weights recomputes the queue; changes persist across sessions.

#### US-5: Override the ranking when I disagree
- As a user, I want to pin a task to the top, so that the system does not hide something I must do now.
- Acceptance Criteria: A pin places the task at rank 1 (FR-6); the pinned task is visually marked (FR-8); removing the pin restores automatic ordering.

#### US-6: Time-box my override
- As a user, I want an override to expire, so that I do not leave stale pins that distort my queue forever.
- Acceptance Criteria: An override may be indefinite, until a date/time, or until completion (FR-7); on expiry the task returns to its computed rank automatically.

#### US-7: Escalate genuine deadlines
- As a user with a hard deadline, I want urgent tasks to rise as the deadline approaches, so that I don't miss commitments.
- Acceptance Criteria: Deadline proximity increases urgency in the score (FR-9); a task past due is never buried below a non-urgent task solely by age or effort.

#### US-8: Respect dependency order
- As a user, I want a task blocked by an unfinished dependency to rank below its blocker, so that I don't start work I can't finish.
- Acceptance Criteria: A blocked task is ranked below its unfinished blockers; completing the blocker updates both tasks' ranks.

#### US-9: See an empty queue gracefully
- As a new user, I want a helpful prompt when nothing is active, so that I am not confused by a blank screen.
- Acceptance Criteria: An empty "Today" state shows an explanation and a call-to-action to add a task.

#### US-10: Stay responsive with a large backlog
- As a heavy user, I want the queue to load and reorder quickly, so that prioritization never slows me down.
- Acceptance Criteria: The queue renders within the product-wide performance targets for realistic list sizes; reordering after an edit is visible within 100 ms of acknowledgement.

#### US-11: Operate the queue by keyboard
- As a keyboard user, I want to navigate and pin/unpin without a mouse, so that I can work efficiently.
- Acceptance Criteria: All queue actions (open, pin, override, remove override) are reachable and operable by keyboard with visible focus.

### F-2 — Quick Add

#### US-12: Capture a task in one line
- As a user with a fleeting thought, I want to add a task by typing one line and pressing Enter, so that capture never interrupts my flow.
- Acceptance Criteria: A single mandatory free-text field exists (FR-26); one confirm action creates the task; the input is reachable from every primary screen.

#### US-13: Use natural language for due dates
- As a user, I want to type "tomorrow 5pm" and have it understood, so that I don't open a date picker.
- Acceptance Criteria: Recognized expressions bind to the task's due date/time (FR-27); the resolved value is shown before confirmation.

#### US-14: Mark importance inline
- As a user, I want to type "!!" or "urgent" to flag importance, so that the task feeds prioritization correctly.
- Acceptance Criteria: Markers map to the explicit-importance field consumed by F-1 (FR-28); the marker is removed from the title.

#### US-15: Tag and contextualize inline
- As a user, I want to type "#work" and "@home", so that tasks are organized as I capture them.
- Acceptance Criteria: `#tag` and `@context` tokens attach to the task (FR-29); unrecognized tokens remain in the title.

#### US-16: Preview what will be parsed
- As a cautious user, I want to see how my line will be interpreted before I commit, so that I can catch mistakes.
- Acceptance Criteria: Interpreted fields (title, due date/time, priority, tags) are previewed before confirmation (FR-30).

#### US-17: Correct a misparse
- As a user, I want to edit a parsed field in place, so that a wrong interpretation does not become a wrong task.
- Acceptance Criteria: Each parsed field is editable before confirmation; edited values override the parser output.

#### US-18: Fall back safely on unparseable input
- As a user typing something unusual, I want the whole line kept as the title if nothing parses, so that I never lose input.
- Acceptance Criteria: When no tokens are recognized, the full line becomes the title and no fields are invented.

#### US-19: Resolve ambiguity predictably
- As a user, I want ambiguous phrases handled consistently, so that behavior is learnable.
- Acceptance Criteria: Ambiguous expressions follow a documented rule (e.g. nearest future occurrence); the chosen interpretation is shown in the preview.

#### US-20: Undo an accidental add
- As a user, I want to undo a just-created task, so that a slip does not clutter my list.
- Acceptance Criteria: A confirmation affords undo for a short window; undo removes the created task entirely.

#### US-21: Respect my timezone
- As a traveler, I want parsed times interpreted in my current timezone, so that "5pm" means 5pm where I am.
- Acceptance Criteria: Parsed times use the user's effective timezone; a timezone change re-renders existing due times consistently.

#### US-22: Capture while offline
- As a user on a flaky connection, I want quick add to work offline, so that capture is never blocked.
- Acceptance Criteria: The task is accepted locally and clearly marked as pending sync; it syncs without duplication when connectivity returns.

#### US-23: Avoid accidental duplicates
- As a user, I want a warning when I add a near-identical open task, so that I don't create clutter.
- Acceptance Criteria: A near-duplicate warning appears before commit; the user can confirm or cancel.

#### US-24: Complete the flow by keyboard only
- As a keyboard user, I want to open, preview, and confirm quick add without a mouse, so that capture stays fast.
- Acceptance Criteria: The entire quick-add flow is keyboard-operable with visible focus and sensible tab order.

### F-3 — Focus Mode

#### US-25: Start focusing on a task
- As a user, I want to begin a focus session from a task, so that I commit a block of time to it.
- Acceptance Criteria: A session can start from the task detail view, the "Today" queue (from F-1 ids are plain-text references), or a quick-add result (from F-2 ids are plain-text references) (FR-51).

#### US-26: Use my preferred session length
- As a user, I want a default session length I can rely on, so that starting focus requires no setup.
- Acceptance Criteria: A configurable default (built-in 25 minutes) applies (FR-52); the default persists across sessions.

#### US-27: Set a custom duration
- As a user with a longer task, I want to set a custom length, so that the timer matches my work.
- Acceptance Criteria: Custom durations within the supported range (per feature validation V-1 in this feature file) are accepted before or during a session (FR-53).

#### US-28: Control the timer
- As a user, I want to pause, resume, extend, and end, so that the session fits reality.
- Acceptance Criteria: All controls exist and update the UI immediately (FR-54); paused time is not counted as focused time.

#### US-29: Never run two sessions at once
- As a user, I want clear handling when a session is already active, so that my time records stay accurate.
- Acceptance Criteria: Starting a new session while one is active forces an explicit decision (per business rule BR-3 in this feature file) (FR-55).

#### US-30: See my session at a glance
- As a user, I want an unambiguous on-screen timer, so that I know how long remains.
- Acceptance Criteria: Remaining time is legible, updates at least once per second, and is visible without scrolling.

#### US-31: Work without distraction
- As a user, I want a distraction-free surface during focus, so that I stay on one task.
- Acceptance Criteria: Non-essential chrome is suppressed during a session; the focused task's title remains visible.

#### US-32: Be reminded when time is up
- As a user, I want a clear end-of-session signal, so that I can transition deliberately.
- Acceptance Criteria: Session completion produces a noticeable, dismissible signal; the user is offered stop or extend.

#### US-33: Know focused time was recorded
- As a user, I want focus time attributed to the task, so that my history reflects the effort.
- Acceptance Criteria: Completed (and per policy, paused/ended) sessions record focused duration against the task (FR-56 onward in this feature file).

#### US-34: End a session early
- As a user, I want to stop before time is up, so that an interrupted block is not lost.
- Acceptance Criteria: Ending early records elapsed time; the task is not auto-completed without confirmation.

#### US-35: Keep the timer accurate in the background
- As a user, I want the timer to stay correct if I switch tabs, so that the app doesn't drift.
- Acceptance Criteria: Elapsed time is derived from wall-clock timestamps, not tick counting, so it is correct after backgrounding.

#### US-36: Recover from an interrupted session
- As a user whose app closed mid-session, I want a sane recovery, so that nothing is silently lost.
- Acceptance Criteria: On return, the session is either restored or the user is prompted; no session remains "running" with no UI.

#### US-37: Review my focus history
- As a user, I want to see past sessions, so that I can understand my patterns.
- Acceptance Criteria: A history list shows task, date, planned and actual duration for each session.

#### US-38: Operate focus mode accessibly
- As a user relying on assistive tech, I want the timer and controls accessible, so that I can use focus mode fully.
- Acceptance Criteria: Timer changes are announced politely, controls have accessible names, and no flashing exceeds safe limits.

### F-4 — Progress Analytics

#### US-39: Reach my progress view
- As a user, I want a dedicated Progress view, so that I can review how I am doing in one place.
- Acceptance Criteria: The view is reachable from primary navigation and presents personal metrics on one scrollable surface (FR-76).

#### US-40: See completion at a glance
- As a user, I want to see completed, created, and net change, so that I understand my throughput.
- Acceptance Criteria: Completed, created, and net (created − completed) are shown for the selected period (FR-77).

#### US-41: Track completion rate over time
- As a user, I want completion rate plotted over time, so that I can spot trends.
- Acceptance Criteria: Completion rate (completed ÷ created, as a percentage) is plotted at a granularity implied by the period (FR-78).

#### US-42: See my throughput
- As a user, I want to see tasks completed per day/week/month, so that I can gauge capacity.
- Acceptance Criteria: Throughput series are computed and displayed for the selected period (FR-79).

#### US-43: Keep my streak visible
- As a user motivated by streaks, I want current and longest streak shown, so that I stay consistent.
- Acceptance Criteria: Current and longest streak are shown for completing at least one task per day (FR-80).

#### US-44: Choose the period
- As a user, I want to change the time window, so that I can look at a week, month, or year.
- Acceptance Criteria: Period selection updates every metric and chart on the page consistently.

#### US-45: Inspect a data point
- As a user, I want exact values on demand, so that a chart is not the only source of truth.
- Acceptance Criteria: Hovering or tapping a series reveals the precise values and date for that point.

#### US-46: See a helpful empty state
- As a new user, I want guidance when there is no data yet, so that I don't think analytics are broken.
- Acceptance Criteria: No-data periods show an explanation and a call-to-action, not empty or broken charts.

#### US-47: Access analytics non-visually
- As a screen-reader user, I want the metrics available as text, so that charts are not a barrier.
- Acceptance Criteria: Every chart has a textual or table equivalent carrying the same values.

#### US-48: Keep day boundaries correct
- As a user, I want my analytics to respect my timezone, so that "today" means my today.
- Acceptance Criteria: Day-based metrics use the user's effective timezone; a timezone change does not retroactively shift historical records.

#### US-49: Keep analytics fresh
- As a user, I want metrics to reflect recent activity, so that the view is trustworthy.
- Acceptance Criteria: Metrics update after task completion within the product-wide interaction targets; the view indicates when it last refreshed.

#### US-50: Export my data
- As a user, I want to export my metrics, so that I can keep or share a record.
- Acceptance Criteria: A structured export (e.g. CSV) of the selected period is produced matching the on-screen values.

#### US-51: Keep analytics private
- As an individual user, I want my progress to be visible only to me, so that personal data stays personal.
- Acceptance Criteria: Analytics are scoped to the signed-in user; no other user can retrieve them.

### F-5 — Integration Hub

#### US-52: Browse what I can connect
- As a user, I want a catalogue of source types, so that I know what is possible before committing.
- Acceptance Criteria: The catalogue lists connectable types with plain-language read/write descriptions (FR-101).

#### US-53: Connect an account safely
- As a user, I want to authorize a provider without typing my password into the app, so that my credentials stay safe.
- Acceptance Criteria: Connection uses a provider authorization handshake; the connection appears only after a successful callback (FR-102).

#### US-54: Manage existing connections
- As a user, I want to see and control my connections, so that I stay in charge of what is linked.
- Acceptance Criteria: A list shows label, type, account identity, state, and last-sync time, and supports lifecycle actions (FR-103).

#### US-55: Label my connections
- As a user with several accounts, I want to rename them, so that I can tell them apart.
- Acceptance Criteria: Connection labels can be set and edited and are shown everywhere the connection appears.

#### US-56: Pause and resume syncing
- As a user, I want to pause a connection, so that I can stop data flow without disconnecting.
- Acceptance Criteria: Pausing halts sync while preserving configuration; resuming restores sync without re-authorizing.

#### US-57: Recover an expired connection
- As a user whose token expired, I want a clear reconnect path, so that syncing resumes with minimal effort.
- Acceptance Criteria: Expired/error states are visible with a prominent reconnect action; successful reconnect clears the error state.

#### US-58: Disconnect completely
- As a user, I want to disconnect, so that no further data is read or written.
- Acceptance Criteria: Disconnecting revokes stored credentials and stops sync; the remaining imported data policy is stated to the user before confirming.

#### US-59: Know sync status
- As a user, I want last-sync time and state visible, so that I can tell whether data is current.
- Acceptance Criteria: Every connection shows its state (`connected`, `degraded`, `expired`, `error`, `paused`, `disconnected`) and last-sync time.

#### US-60: Understand a degraded integration
- As a user, I want plain-language errors, so that I know whether to retry or reconnect.
- Acceptance Criteria: Degraded/error states explain the cause in plain language and offer the appropriate recovery action.

#### US-61: Import work from a source
- As a user, I want items from a connected source to become tasks, so that my external work appears in one place.
- Acceptance Criteria: Items from a read-capable source are imported with source attribution; duplicates are not created on repeat syncs.

#### US-62: Write back to a source
- As a user, I want supported changes to sync outward, so that I don't maintain two systems.
- Acceptance Criteria: For write-capable sources, supported changes (e.g. completion) propagate outward; failures surface as connection errors.

#### US-63: Resolve sync conflicts predictably
- As a user with two-way sync, I want conflicts handled by a clear rule, so that data doesn't silently diverge.
- Acceptance Criteria: A documented conflict rule applies deterministically; when the rule cannot decide, the user is asked.

#### US-64: Protect my credentials
- As a security-conscious user, I want tokens stored and handled securely, so that a breach doesn't expose my accounts.
- Acceptance Criteria: Credentials are stored in an encrypted secret store, never in client-readable plaintext, and are revocable per connection.

#### US-65: Use an accessible connector UI
- As a user with assistive tech, I want the connection list and its actions accessible, so that I can manage integrations.
- Acceptance Criteria: Connection states are announced, actions have accessible names, and empty/error states are readable.

### F-6 — Dark Mode

#### US-66: Pick my theme
- As a user, I want to choose light, dark, or system, so that the app suits my environment.
- Acceptance Criteria: Exactly one of `light`, `dark`, `system` is selectable and governs the whole product (FR-126).

#### US-67: Follow my system setting
- As a user, I want the app to follow my OS theme, so that it matches everything else on my device.
- Acceptance Criteria: On `system`, the effective theme resolves from the OS/browser signal and re-resolves live on change, without reload (FR-127).

#### US-68: Keep my choice next time
- As a user, I want my preference remembered, so that I don't re-select it every session.
- Acceptance Criteria: The preference persists across reload, sign-out/sign-in, and full restart on the same device (FR-128).

#### US-69: Switch instantly
- As a user, I want switching to be immediate, so that nothing looks half-updated.
- Acceptance Criteria: Changing the preference or the system signal re-themes every rendered surface without a reload (FR-129).

#### US-70: Avoid a flash of the wrong theme
- As a user, I want no bright flash on load in dark mode, so that the app doesn't dazzle me.
- Acceptance Criteria: The correct theme is applied before first paint; no light-to-dark flash occurs on reload.

#### US-71: Read comfortably in both themes
- As a user, I want sufficient contrast in either theme, so that content stays legible.
- Acceptance Criteria: Text and UI elements meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast in both themes.

#### US-72: Keep imagery and charts consistent
- As a user, I want visuals tuned per theme, so that nothing becomes unreadable or jarring.
- Acceptance Criteria: Images, illustrations, and chart palettes have theme-appropriate variants; no chart series becomes indistinguishable.

#### US-73: Print and export sensibly
- As a user printing a page, I want legible output regardless of theme, so that documents are usable.
- Acceptance Criteria: Print styles use an appropriate ink-saving palette independent of the screen theme.

#### US-74: Keep my theme across devices
- As a signed-in user, I want my theme to follow me, so that each device feels consistent.
- Acceptance Criteria: When signed in, the preference is stored with the account and applied on other devices; the local choice wins only when the user is offline.

#### US-75: Theme every state
- As a user, I want error, empty, and loading states themed too, so that nothing breaks the look.
- Acceptance Criteria: Error, empty, loading, and modal surfaces are fully themed in both themes.

## API Contracts

This section defines the functional, transport-level contracts for every feature F-1 .. F-6. Protocol binding (REST/GraphQL, sync vs. async delivery, storage engine, auth mechanism) is the Architect's decision; the contracts below state the observable behaviour the implementation must satisfy. No technology, framework, database, or vendor is selected here.

`API-` ids are local to this section, numbered sequentially from 1 and grouped by feature. `FR-`, `NFR-`, and `US-` ids are global and are referenced as plain text only — never re-defined.

### 0. Scope map

| Feature | API ids | Contracts | Traces to |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-1 Intelligent Task Prioritization | API-1 .. API-9 | 9 | FR-1 .. FR-25 range (FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-6, FR-7, FR-8, FR-9) |
| F-2 Quick Add | API-10 .. API-14 | 5 | FR-26 .. FR-30 range |
| F-3 Focus Mode | API-15 .. API-20 | 6 | FR-51 .. FR-56 range |
| F-4 Progress Analytics | API-21 .. API-25 | 5 | FR-76 .. FR-80 range |
| F-5 Integration Hub | API-26 .. API-35 | 10 | FR-101 .. FR-103 range |
| F-6 Dark Mode | API-36 .. API-39 | 4 | FR-126 .. FR-129 range |

### 1. Cross-cutting API conventions

| Convention | Contract |
|---|---|
| Base path & versioning | All contracts are served under a single versioned prefix (`/v1`). Changes are additive within a version; removals or semantic changes require a new version. Deprecations are announced with at least 12 months' notice and expose a `Deprecation` / `Sunset` response header. |
| Payload format | JSON request and response bodies, UTF-8. `Content-Type: application/json`. Responses that carry no body return no body (not an empty JSON object). |
| Identifiers | All entity ids are opaque strings. Clients must not parse meaning out of them, and ids are never reused. |
| Timestamps | All timestamps are UTC, ISO-8601 with offset. User-local display values are derived from the user's IANA timezone, never from a server-local clock. |
| Clock authority | For any timed feature (F-3 sessions, F-1 urgency, F-2 relative dates) the server clock is authoritative. Time-sensitive responses carry a `serverTime` field so a client with a skewed clock can self-correct. |
| Authorization scoping | Every endpoint operates strictly on data owned by the authenticated principal. There is no contract that reads or mutates another user's rows. Unauthenticated calls return `401`; authenticated calls that target out-of-scope resources return `404` (never `403` for existence-leaking resources) or `403` where existence is already known to the caller. |
| Error envelope | Every non-2xx response body uses one shape: `{ "error": { "code": "<stable_machine_code>", "message": "<human readable>", "field": "<optional field path>", "details": { }, "requestId": "<traceable id>", "retryable": <bool> } }`. `code` values are stable strings (e.g. `invalid_weight_set`, `session_already_active`, `reconnect_required`). `requestId` is echoed in the response header for support correlation. |
| Status codes in use | `200` OK, `201` Created, `202` Accepted (async work queued), `204` No Content, `207` Multi-Status (batch results), `400` malformed request, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` unknown or out-of-scope, `409` state conflict, `410` gone/expired, `412` precondition failed, `413` payload too large, `422` semantically invalid, `429` rate limited, `500` unexpected server error, `502` upstream provider failure, `503` temporarily unavailable. |
| Idempotency | Every state-changing `POST`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header. A replay with the same key and body returns the original status and body for 24 hours; a replay with the same key and a different body returns `409 idempotency_key_reuse`. |
| Concurrency control | Mutable resources expose an `ETag` and accept `If-Match` on mutation. A stale `If-Match` returns `412 stale_precondition` with the current representation in the error `details`. |
| Pagination | Cursor-based: request `?limit=&cursor=`, response `{ "items": [...], "nextCursor": "<opaque|null>" }`. Default `limit` 50, maximum 200; `limit` outside range returns `422 invalid_limit`; a malformed or expired cursor returns `422 invalid_cursor`. |
| Rate limiting | `429` responses carry `Retry-After` and the rate-limit headers. Interactive endpoints (F-2 quick add, F-3 session controls, F-6 preference writes) are rate limited per principal and must remain usable under burst while bulk/analytics endpoints are limited more tightly. |
| Freshness disclosure | Derived reads (ranking, analytics, sync state) return the instant they were computed plus a freshness value, so a client can label stale data instead of silently showing it as current. |
| Secrets | No response body, error detail, log line, or analytics payload ever contains a provider credential, refresh token, or authorization code. Integration credentials are write-only: accepted (if at all) only through the handshake in API-27/API-28 and never read back. |
| Audit | Every mutation records actor, entity, before/after values where applicable, and timestamp. Audit records are readable by the owning principal on request; they are never silently discarded. |
| Domain events | Successful mutations emit an internal event (`task.created`, `task.completed`, `focus_session.completed`, `integration.connection_state_changed`, `integration.sync.completed`, `preference.theme_changed`) that downstream features consume — F-4 analytics consumes task and focus-session events; F-1 rank recomputation consumes task mutations. Event delivery is at-least-once; consumers must be idempotent. |

---

### 2. F-1 — Intelligent Task Prioritization — API Contracts

| ID | Method / Path | Purpose (traces) | Request (key fields) | Success | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-1 | `GET /v1/tasks?state=active&sort=priority&limit=&cursor=` | Ranked "Today" queue of active tasks by descending score (FR-2) | `state` (default `active`), `sort`, `limit`, `cursor`, optional `projectId`, `tag` | `200 { "items": [ { "taskId", "title", "priorityScore", "rank", "factors": { "dueUrgency", "importance", "effort", "age", "dependencyState" }, "override": { … } \| null, "dueAt" } ], "nextCursor", "computedAt", "profileVersion" }` — order is stable across identical reads | `400 invalid_sort`, `422 invalid_limit`, `422 invalid_cursor`, `401` |
| API-2 | `GET /v1/tasks/{taskId}/priority` | Per-task score with factor breakdown (FR-1, FR-3, FR-9) | Path `taskId`; optional `at=<timestamp>` to evaluate the score at a past/future instant | `200 { "taskId", "score", "rank", "computedAt", "profileVersion", "factors": [ { "name", "rawValue", "normalisedValue", "weight", "contribution" } ], "effectiveUrgency", "escalationActive": <bool> }` | `404 unknown_task`, `409 task_not_active` (completed/deleted task has no live score), `422 invalid_at` |
| API-3 | `GET /v1/tasks/{taskId}/priority/explanation` | Plain-language reason for the current rank (FR-5) | Path `taskId`; optional `locale` | `200 { "taskId", "summary": "<one sentence>", "dominantFactors": [ { "name", "text" } ], "overrideNote": "<string|null>", "generatedAt", "profileVersion", "locale" }`. Text must name dominant factors in the user's language without internal jargon, weights, or raw scores. | `404 unknown_task`, `409 task_not_active`, `406 unsupported_locale` |
| API-4 | `GET /v1/me/prioritization-profile` | Read current factor weights (FR-4) | — | `200 { "profileVersion", "weights": { "dueUrgency", "importance", "effort", "age", "dependencyState" }, "updatedAt" }` | `401` |
| API-5 | `PUT /v1/me/prioritization-profile` | Set relative factor weights (FR-4) | `{ "weights": { … }, "ifVersion": <int> }`; each weight numeric in a fixed supported band, at least one weight strictly positive | `200` new profile with incremented `profileVersion`; the queue is recomputed asynchronously (see API-8) | `422 invalid_weight_set` (unknown factor, negative, all-zero), `412 stale_precondition` (`ifVersion` mismatch, `details.current` returned), `401` |
| API-6 | `POST /v1/tasks/{taskId}/overrides` | Create a pin or forced rank position (FR-6, FR-7) | `{ "mode": "pin" \| "position", "position": <int> \| null, "expiry": { "type": "never" \| "until" \| "onCompletion", "until": <timestamp> \| null } }` | `201 { "overrideId", "taskId", "mode", "requestedPosition", "effectiveRank", "expiresAt": <timestamp\|null>, "createdAt" }`; the task's position in API-1 reflects the override on the next read | `404 unknown_task`, `409 override_exists` (details carries the active override id), `422 invalid_position` (below 1 or beyond queue length + 1), `422 expiry_in_past`, `422 invalid_expiry_type` |
| API-7 | `DELETE /v1/tasks/{taskId}/overrides/{overrideId}` | Remove an override so natural ranking resumes (FR-8) | Path ids | `204`; repeat calls on an already-removed override also return `204` (idempotent) | `404 unknown_task`, `404 unknown_override` |
| API-8 | `POST /v1/prioritization/recomputations` | Request a full rescore of the principal's active tasks (FR-1, FR-2) | `{ "reason": "manual" \| "profile_change" \| "bulk_edit", "scope": "all_active" }` | `202 { "jobId", "scope", "requestedAt", "estimatedCompletion" }` | `409 recomputation_in_progress` (details carries the running `jobId`), `401` |
| API-9 | `GET /v1/prioritization/recomputations/{jobId}` | Poll recomputation status (FR-1) | Path `jobId` | `200 { "jobId", "status": "queued" \| "running" \| "succeeded" \| "failed", "tasksRescored", "startedAt", "finishedAt", "error": <error envelope \| null> }` | `404 unknown_job`, `401` |

**Ordering guarantees (F-1).** API-1 order is deterministic for identical inputs and identical profile version: ties break on due date ascending, then explicit importance descending, then creation time ascending. A task with an active `pin` override is always returned at rank 1; a task with a `position` override occupies the requested rank and all other tasks shift down without reordering among themselves.

**Consistency (F-1).** API-1 and API-2 may serve a read that is up to a bounded staleness behind the most recent mutation; the bound and the `computedAt` value are the contract. After API-8 reports `succeeded`, subsequent reads must reflect the new profile.

### 3. F-2 — Quick Add — API Contracts

| ID | Method / Path | Purpose (traces) | Request (key fields) | Success | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-10 | `POST /v1/quick-add/parse` | Dry-run interpretation of one free-text line; nothing is persisted (FR-30) | `{ "text": "<line>", "timezone": "<IANA>", "now": <timestamp\|null> }` | `200 { "title", "dueAt": <timestamp\|null>, "importance": <int\|null>, "tags": [ … ], "projectId": <string\|null>, "contexts": [ … ], "parseWarnings": [ { "code", "token", "message" } ], "unparsedTokens": [ … ] }`. Tokens that are not recognised remain part of `title`. | `400 empty_input`, `413 input_too_long` (limit 500 characters), `422 invalid_timezone`, `401` |
| API-11 | `POST /v1/quick-add` | Single-confirm capture: parse and create in one call (FR-26, FR-27, FR-28, FR-29) | `{ "text": "<line>", "timezone": "<IANA>", "overrides": { "title"?, "dueAt"?, "importance"?, "tags"?, "projectId"? } }` + `Idempotency-Key` | `201 { "taskId", "title", "dueAt", "importance", "tags", "projectId", "state": "active", "parsedFields": <same shape as API-10>, "warnings": [ … ], "createdAt" }` | `400 empty_input`, `413 input_too_long`, `422 invalid_timezone`, `422 invalid_override` (explicit override contradicts the parser contract, e.g. malformed timestamp), `409 idempotency_key_reuse`, `401` |
| API-12 | `POST /v1/quick-add/{draftId}/confirm` | Two-step variant: commit a previewed draft the user may have edited (FR-30) | `{ "accepted": { "title", "dueAt", "importance", "tags", "projectId" } }` | `201` task payload identical in shape to API-11 | `404 unknown_draft`, `410 draft_expired` (draft TTL is 15 minutes and is returned as `expiresAt` when the draft is created), `409 draft_already_confirmed` (details carries the created `taskId`), `422 invalid_field` |
| API-13 | `DELETE /v1/tasks/{taskId}?reason=quick_add_undo` | Undo an accidental capture inside the undo window (FR-26) | Path `taskId`, query `reason` | `204`; repeat calls return `204` (idempotent) | `409 undo_window_expired` (the task may still be deleted through normal deletion), `403 undo_not_applicable` (task was created by a path other than quick add), `404 unknown_task` |
| API-14 | `POST /v1/quick-add/batch` | Replay a client-side capture queue captured while offline | `{ "items": [ { "clientItemId", "text", "capturedAt", "timezone" } ] }`, max 100 items, each with its own idempotency basis on `clientItemId` | `207 { "results": [ { "clientItemId", "status": "created" \| "duplicate" \| "rejected", "taskId": <string\|null>, "warnings": [ … ], "error": <error envelope\|null> } ] }` — a partial failure never rejects the whole batch | `413 batch_too_large`, `422 too_many_items`, `401` |

**Capture guarantees (F-2).** An unparseable or ambiguous date/time expression is **never** a creation failure: the field is left unset, the token stays in the title, and the response carries a `parseWarnings` entry (API-10, API-11). Only structurally invalid input (empty text, over-length text, invalid timezone, invalid explicit override) is rejected. The `dueAt` value returned for relative expressions such as "in 2 hours" is resolved against the server clock at creation time and returned absolute, so it is stable across later reads.

### 4. F-3 — Focus Mode — API Contracts

| ID | Method / Path | Purpose (traces) | Request (key fields) | Success | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-15 | `POST /v1/focus-sessions` | Start a session bound to one task (FR-51, FR-52, FR-53, FR-55) | `{ "taskId", "plannedMinutes": <int\|null>, "startImmediately": <bool> }` + `Idempotency-Key` | `201 { "sessionId", "taskId", "state": "running" \| "paused", "plannedMinutes", "startedAt", "elapsedSeconds", "remainingSeconds", "serverTime", "expiresAt" }` | `404 unknown_task`, `409 session_already_active` (details carries `activeSessionId`, `taskId`, `remainingSeconds` so the client can offer the explicit decision in BR-3), `422 duration_out_of_range` (details carries the supported min/max), `401` |
| API-16 | `GET /v1/focus-sessions/active` | Read the single active session, if any (FR-55) | — | `200` session payload identical in shape to API-15, with `serverTime` and `remainingSeconds` recomputed for this read; `204` when no session is active | `401` |
| API-17 | `PATCH /v1/focus-sessions/{id}` | Pause, resume, extend, or end a session (FR-54, FR-56) | `{ "action": "pause" \| "resume" \| "extend" \| "end", "extendMinutes": <int\|null>, "reason": <string\|null> }` | `200` updated session payload including `state`, `elapsedSeconds`, `remainingSeconds`, `serverTime`, and — for `end` — `completedAt`, `actualMinutes`, `outcome`; `extend` returns the new `expiresAt` | `404 unknown_session`, `409 invalid_transition` (e.g. `resume` on an ended session; details names the current state), `410 session_expired` (server-side timer already elapsed before the call arrived), `422 extend_out_of_range`, `401` |
| API-18 | `GET /v1/me/focus-settings` | Read the session defaults and supported band (FR-52, FR-53) | — | `200 { "defaultMinutes", "minMinutes", "maxMinutes", "pauseAllowed": <bool>, "notificationPreference": "in_app" \| "os" \| "both" \| "none", "updatedAt" }` | `401` |
| API-19 | `PUT /v1/me/focus-settings` | Change defaults for future sessions (FR-52, FR-53) | `{ "defaultMinutes", "notificationPreference"? }` | `200` updated settings; `defaultMinutes` must be a whole number inside the supported band | `422 out_of_range` (details carries `minMinutes`/`maxMinutes`), `422 invalid_notification_preference`, `412 stale_precondition`, `401` |
| API-20 | `GET /v1/focus-sessions?taskId=&from=&to=&limit=&cursor=` | Session history for the task and for F-4 rollups | Filters `taskId`, `from`, `to`, `state`; pagination params | `200 { "items": [ { "sessionId", "taskId", "state", "plannedMinutes", "actualMinutes", "startedAt", "endedAt", "outcome" } ], "nextCursor" }` | `422 range_invalid` (`from` after `to`), `422 range_too_wide` (maximum 366 days), `404 unknown_task`, `401` |

**Timer guarantees (F-3).** Session duration is authoritative on the server. Every session response carries `serverTime` and `remainingSeconds`; a client that resumes after sleep reconciles to those values rather than to its local timer. A session that elapses while the client is absent transitions server-side to an ended state and is reported by API-16/API-17 with `state = "ended"` plus its `outcome`, rather than being silently dropped. Only one session per principal may be in a non-ended state (FR-55); the conflict response is the sole path that lets the client start a competing session, and it requires an explicit client decision before it retries.

### 5. F-4 — Progress Analytics — API Contracts

| ID | Method / Path | Purpose (traces) | Request (key fields) | Success | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-21 | `GET /v1/analytics/summary?period=&from=&to=&timezone=` | Single-surface headline metrics (FR-76, FR-77, FR-78) | `period` ∈ `7d \| 30d \| 90d \| custom`; `from`/`to` required when `custom`; `timezone` required (IANA) | `200 { "period": { "from", "to", "granularity" }, "timezone", "created": <int>, "completed": <int>, "net": <int>, "completionRate": <decimal 0..1>, "completionRateSeries": [ { "bucketStart", "value" } ], "tasksCompletedPerBucket": [ { "bucketStart", "value" } ], "computedAt", "dataFreshnessSeconds" }` | `422 invalid_period`, `422 range_invalid`, `422 range_too_wide` (366-day maximum), `422 invalid_timezone`, `422 range_in_future` (`from` after now), `401` |
| API-22 | `GET /v1/analytics/completion-rate?granularity=&from=&to=&timezone=` | Completion-rate time series (FR-78) | `granularity` ∈ `day \| week \| month`, `from`, `to`, `timezone` | `200 { "granularity", "timezone", "series": [ { "bucketStart", "bucketEnd", "completed", "created", "rate" } ], "computedAt" }` | `422 granularity_not_supported_for_range` (e.g. `day` over more than 92 days), `422 range_invalid`, `422 invalid_timezone`, `401` |
| API-23 | `GET /v1/analytics/throughput?granularity=&from=&to=&timezone=` | Tasks completed per day/week/month (FR-79) | Same shape as API-22 | `200 { "granularity", "timezone", "series": [ { "bucketStart", "bucketEnd", "completed" } ], "computedAt" }` | Same as API-22 |
| API-24 | `GET /v1/analytics/streaks?timezone=` | Current and longest completion streaks (FR-80) | `timezone` (required) | `200 { "currentStreakDays", "currentStreakStart": <date\|null>, "longestStreakDays", "longestStreakRange": { "from", "to" } \| null, "asOfDate", "computedAt" }` | `422 invalid_timezone`, `401` |
| API-25 | `GET /v1/analytics/export?period=&from=&to=&timezone=&format=` | Export the metrics or the underlying task events for the selected period | `format` ∈ declared set, `Content-Type`-negotiated | `200` streaming document when the result fits the synchronous limit; otherwise `202 { "jobId", "estimatedCompletion" }` plus a status read at `/v1/analytics/export/{jobId}` | `422 unsupported_format`, `422 range_too_wide`, `422 invalid_timezone`, `429 export_rate_limited`, `401` |

**Read-only and completeness guarantees (F-4).** Every analytics contract is read-only. A period with no activity returns `200` with zero-filled buckets — never `404` and never a missing series. A `to` value in the future is clamped to the request time and the clamped value is echoed in `period`. All bucket boundaries are computed in the caller's declared timezone, and the timezone used is always echoed so a client can verify the day boundary it is displaying. `dataFreshnessSeconds` is disclosed so a stale dashboard is labelled rather than presented as live. Task, completion, and focus-session inputs to these aggregates are consumed from the domain events declared in §1; the underlying task and session records remain owned by F-1, F-2, and F-3.

### 6. F-5 — Integration Hub — API Contracts

| ID | Method / Path | Purpose (traces) | Request (key fields) | Success | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-26 | `GET /v1/integrations/catalogue` | Browsable catalogue of connectable source types (FR-101) | Optional `type` filter | `200 { "items": [ { "type", "displayName", "description", "capabilities": { "read": [ … ], "write": [ … ] }, "handshake": "redirect", "scopes": [ … ], "requiredFields": [ … ], "availability": "available" \| "unavailable" } ] }` — description states in plain language what data is read and written | `401` |
| API-27 | `POST /v1/integrations/connections` | Begin the authorization handshake for a source type (FR-102) | `{ "type", "label" }` + `Idempotency-Key` | `201 { "connectionId", "state": "pending_authorization", "authorizationUrl", "stateTokenExpiresAt" }`; the connection is **not** listed as connected until API-28 completes successfully | `422 unknown_type`, `422 provider_unavailable`, `422 credentials_not_accepted` (any provider credential field in the body is rejected by design), `409 connection_already_pending`, `401` |
| API-28 | `GET /v1/integrations/callback?state=&code=&error=` | Complete the handshake and materialise the connection (FR-102) | `state` (single-use, expires), `code` or `error` from the provider | Redirect to the application with a success marker and the `connectionId`; the connection then appears in API-29 with state `connected`, `accountIdentity`, and `lastSyncAt` | `400 invalid_state` (unknown, replayed, or expired), `400 missing_code`, `403 principal_mismatch`, `502 provider_exchange_failed` (no connection is created; the caller may start again with API-27), `409 duplicate_connection` (details carries the existing `connectionId`) |
| API-29 | `GET /v1/integrations/connections` | List connections with identity, state, and last sync (FR-103) | Optional `state` filter, pagination params | `200 { "items": [ { "connectionId", "type", "label", "accountIdentity", "state": "connected" \| "degraded" \| "expired" \| "error" \| "paused" \| "disconnected", "lastSyncAt": <timestamp\|null>, "lastError": { "code", "message", "at" } \| null, "scopes", "pausedAt": <timestamp\|null> } ], "nextCursor" }` — never returns tokens or secrets | `422 invalid_state`, `401` |
| API-30 | `PATCH /v1/integrations/connections/{id}` | Rename, pause, or resume a connection (FR-103) | `{ "label"?: <string>, "state"?: "paused" \| "active" }` | `200` updated connection payload (shape of API-29 item) | `404 unknown_connection`, `422 invalid_label`, `409 reconnect_required` (resuming an `expired` or `error` connection), `409 invalid_transition` (e.g. `active` on a `disconnected` connection), `412 stale_precondition`, `401` |
| API-31 | `POST /v1/integrations/connections/{id}/reconnect` | Re-run the handshake for an existing connection (FR-103) | `{ "label"? }` + `Idempotency-Key` | `201 { "connectionId", "state": "pending_authorization", "authorizationUrl", "stateTokenExpiresAt" }`; the same `connectionId` is retained and its historical sync records are preserved | `404 unknown_connection`, `409 already_connected`, `422 provider_unavailable`, `401` |
| API-32 | `DELETE /v1/integrations/connections/{id}` | Disconnect and revoke access (FR-103) | Path id; optional `?purgeImportedData=<bool>` | `202 { "connectionId", "state": "disconnected", "revocation": { "status": "succeeded" \| "pending", "attemptedAt" } }` — repeat calls return`202` (idempotent; `revocation.status` may advance from `pending` to `succeeded` on a later read) | `404 unknown_connection`, `409 purge_in_progress` (details carries the running purge job id), `401` |
| API-33 | `POST /v1/integrations/connections/{id}/sync` | Trigger a manual sync of an existing connection | `{ "scope": "incremental" \| "full", "reason": "manual" \| "post_reconnect" }` + `Idempotency-Key` | `202 { "syncRunId", "connectionId", "scope", "status": "queued", "requestedAt", "estimatedCompletion" }` | `404 unknown_connection`, `409 sync_in_progress` (details carries the running `syncRunId`), `409 connection_not_syncable` (state is `paused`, `expired`, `error`, or `disconnected`; details names the state and the required recovery action, e.g. API-31), `429 sync_rate_limited` (with `Retry-After`), `502 provider_unavailable` (details carries `retryable: true`), `401` |
| API-34 | `GET /v1/integrations/connections/{id}/sync-runs?status=&limit=&cursor=` | Sync run history with per-run outcome counts and bounded failure detail | Optional `status` filter, pagination params | `200 { "items": [ { "syncRunId", "connectionId", "scope", "status": "queued" \| "running" \| "succeeded" \| "partial" \| "failed", "startedAt", "finishedAt": <timestamp\|null>, "counts": { "read", "created", "updated", "skipped", "failed" }, "failureCount", "failuresTruncated": <bool>, "failures": [ { "itemRef", "code", "message", "retryable", "at" } ], "nextRetryAt": <timestamp\|null> } ], "nextCursor", "computedAt" }` — `failures` is capped and `failuresTruncated` plus `failureCount` disclose the cap | `404 unknown_connection`, `422 invalid_status`, `422 invalid_limit`, `422 invalid_cursor`, `401` |
| API-35 | `POST /v1/integrations/webhooks/{sourceToken}` | Inbound ingestion endpoint for the generic webhook bridge source type; machine-to-machine, single-purpose rotatable token, not a user session | Raw JSON body; `X-Signature` (HMAC over the raw body, constant-time verified), `X-Delivery-Id` (provider-assigned, used for dedupe), optional `X-Timestamp` for replay-window enforcement | `202 { "accepted": true, "duplicate": false, "deliveryId", "connectionId", "receivedAt" }` — ingestion is always asynchronous; a replayed `X-Delivery-Id` within the dedupe window returns `200 { "accepted": true, "duplicate": true, "deliveryId" }` | `401 invalid_signature` (also returned when `X-Timestamp` falls outside the accepted replay window, details carries `reason`), `404 unknown_source_token` (also returned for a revoked token, so revocation is not distinguishable from non-existence), `413 payload_too_large`, `429` (rate limited, with `Retry-After`), `503 ingestion_unavailable` (explicitly `retryable: true` so the provider retries) |

**Integration guarantees (F-5).**

- **No credentials in the product's own fields (FR-102).** API-27 rejects any body containing a provider credential field (`422 credentials_not_accepted`). Credentials exist only inside the handshake completed at API-28 and are never returned by API-29, API-30, API-31, API-34, or any error envelope.
- **Connectivity is asserted only after callback success.** A connection created by API-27 is in `pending_authorization` and is absent from the user-facing "connected" view until API-28 completes. A failed or abandoned handshake leaves no connection and no partial state; `state` tokens are single-use and expire, and a replayed or expired token yields `400 invalid_state`.
- **State is always recoverable, never a dead end.** Every non-`connected` state returned by API-29 maps to a named recovery contract: `expired` and `error` → API-31; `paused` → API-30; `degraded` → API-33 then API-34; `disconnected` → API-27. `lastError` always carries a stable `code`, a human message, and a timestamp, so the UI never has to render an unexplained failure.
- **Partial sync never presents as full success.** A run with mixed results is reported as `partial` with `counts` and a bounded `failures` list (API-34), never as `succeeded`. Retryable failures carry `retryable: true` and `nextRetryAt`.
- **Revocation is attempted and its outcome is disclosed.** API-32 reports `revocation.status` rather than assuming provider-side revocation succeeded, and `purgeImportedData` is opt-in — imported user data is not silently deleted.
- **Inbound ingestion never validates synchronously.** API-35 acknowledges delivery and defers interpretation, so a malformed payload surfaces as a `failed`/`partial` run in API-34 instead of a provider-visible error that would trigger duplicate retries.
- **Identity is never inferred.** `accountIdentity` is supplied by the provider callback; the contract never derives it from a user-entered label.

### 7. F-6 — Dark Mode — API Contracts

| ID | Method / Path | Purpose (traces) | Request (key fields) | Success | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-36 | `GET /v1/me/preferences/theme?systemSignal=light\|dark\|no-preference` | Read the persisted preference and its effective resolution (FR-126, FR-127, FR-128) | Optional `systemSignal` reports the host OS/browser colour-scheme signal observed by the client | `200 { "preference": "light" \| "dark" \| "system", "resolvedTheme": "light" \| "dark" \| null, "resolutionSource": "user_preference" \| "system_signal" \| "account_default", "requiresClientResolution": <bool>, "tokensVersion", "updatedAt", "serverTime" }`. When `preference` is `system` and `systemSignal` is supplied, `resolvedTheme` mirrors it; when `systemSignal` is omitted, `resolvedTheme` is `null` and `requiresClientResolution` is `true` (the server never guesses another device's OS signal). | `422 invalid_system_signal`, `401` |
| API-37 | `PUT /v1/me/preferences/theme` | Set the single whole-product theme preference (FR-126, FR-128, FR-129) | `{ "preference": "light" \| "dark" \| "system", "systemSignal"?: "light" \| "dark" \| "no-preference", "ifVersion"?: <int> }` + `Idempotency-Key` | `200` payload identical in shape to API-36 with the new preference applied and `updatedAt` advanced; the change is durable before the response is sent | `422 invalid_preference` (value outside the closed set), `422 invalid_system_signal`, `412 stale_precondition` (`ifVersion` mismatch; `details.current` returned), `409 idempotency_key_reuse`, `401` |
| API-38 | `GET /v1/theme/tokens?theme=light\|dark&version=` | Read the versioned design-token set for one theme, so every surface themes from one source (FR-129) | `theme` required; optional `version` to pin a known token set | `200 { "theme", "version", "tokens": { "<tokenName>": "<value>" }, "generatedAt" }` with `ETag` and a long-lived `Cache-Control`; `304 Not Modified` on a matching `If-None-Match` | `422 invalid_theme`, `422 unknown_token_version`, `401` (token set is readable only by an authenticated principal) |
| API-39 | `DELETE /v1/me/preferences/theme` | Reset the preference to the account default (`system`) (FR-126, FR-128) | — | `204`; repeat calls also return `204` (idempotent) | `401` |

**Theme guarantees (F-6).**

- **Exactly one preference, product-wide (FR-126).** `preference` is a closed enum of three values and is stored per principal. There is deliberately **no** contract that sets a theme for a single screen, route, or widget — per-surface theming is not expressible in this API.
- **Live system following without a round trip (FR-127).** A change to the host colour-scheme signal is resolved on the client and applied immediately; it does not require a server write and must not trigger a reload. The server participates only to echo `resolvedTheme` when the client chooses to report its signal via `?systemSignal=`.
- **Persistence and flash-free cold start (FR-128).** `preference` is durable server-side and re-applied on the next read after sign-out/sign-in, hard reload, or app restart. Clients may cache the last known `{ preference, resolvedTheme, tokensVersion }` so the correct theme is applied before first paint; a cache miss must fall back to `account_default`, never to a light-only render.
- **Immediate, complete application (FR-129).** API-37 returns the fully resolved state in the same response, and API-38 pins the token set by `version`, so a client can apply the change optimistically and reconcile on the next read without any partially themed state. Because tokens are versioned and `ETag`-cached, a theme change never requires re-deriving colour values per component.
- **No preference is unreachable.** `no-preference` from the system signal is a valid input that surfaces as `account_default` resolution rather than an error.
- **Invalid values are rejected, never coerced.** A preference outside `light|dark|system` is `422 invalid_preference`; the contract never silently substitutes a default, so a client bug cannot silently change a user's theme.

### 8. Cross-contract guarantees

| Guarantee | Contract obligation |
|---|---|
| **Offline tolerance** | Contracts that create or mutate user work are safe to queue client-side and replay: API-11 and API-14 (quick add), API-17 (session control, reconciled against `serverTime`), API-37 (theme). Every replayable call is idempotent by `Idempotency-Key` or by the client-supplied item id in API-14. Read contracts (API-1, API-21..API-25, API-29, API-34, API-36) are safe to serve from cache but must carry and display their `computedAt`/`dataFreshnessSeconds`/`updatedAt` value rather than presenting cached data as live. |
| **No cross-principal access** | Every endpoint is scoped to the authenticated principal; the webhook ingress (API-35) authenticates by scoped token, not by session, and yields no read access to any other principal's data. |
| **No secret egress** | No contract returns provider credentials, access/refresh tokens, signing keys, or source tokens. Tokens are write-only or single-use, and appear in no error envelope, `details` object, or log-correlated `requestId` payload. |
| **Stable machine codes** | Every `4xx`/`5xx` carries a `code` from §1 plus a `retryable` boolean. Clients branch on `code` and `retryable`; human-readable `message` is never parsed. |
| **Explicit freshness** | Derived reads (`priorityScore`, `rank`, analytics buckets, `lastSyncAt`, `resolvedTheme`) always disclose when the value was computed. The API never presents a derived value without its computation instant. |
| **Reversible user actions** | Actions with destructive or surprising effects are reversible through a contract: quick-add capture (API-13), override removal (API-7), disconnect without purge (API-32), theme reset (API-39). |
| **Bounded work** | List reads are paginated (§1), sync failure detail is capped with a truncation flag (API-34), and analytics/export ranges are bounded with an explicit `422` rather than a silent partial result (API-21..API-25). |
| **Feature coverage** | Every contract above belongs to exactly one feature and only reuses ids within its own range: F-1 → API-1..API-9, F-2 → API-10..API-14, F-3 → API-15..API-20, F-4 → API-21..API-25, F-5 → API-26..API-35, F-6 → API-36..API-39. |

### 9. API-level open questions

These are scoped to this section and are for the user to decide; they are not resolved by this contract set.

| ID | Question | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| OQ-1 | Should the theme preference be per-principal (shared across that user's devices) or per-device? | FR-128 requires persistence on the same device and is satisfied either way; a per-principal model makes a preference follow the user across devices, while a per-device model requires additional client-local storage semantics not expressed in API-36/API-37. |
| OQ-2 | Should a focus session that elapses server-side while the client is offline be recorded as `completed` or as `abandoned`? | API-17 and API-20 both surface an `outcome` field, but the value set is not fixed by FR-54/FR-56. |
| OQ-3 | Should quick-add undo (API-13) be exposed as a single most-recent action or as a short, addressable history? | FR-26 specifies one confirm action; the undo window duration and depth are not specified upstream. |
| OQ-4 | Should a `position` override (API-6) be allowed beyond the current queue length? | API-6 currently rejects positions below 1 or beyond queue length + 1; permitting far-future positions would require the contract to define what happens when the queue grows or shrinks. |
| OQ-5 | Is a completion streak (FR-80) measured in calendar days in the user's timezone only, or may a user choose a custom day boundary? | API-24 requires a `timezone` and computes in it; a custom boundary would widen the contract. |

## Design Direction

The product reads as a **calm, high-signal personal command center** — the visual opposite of a noisy kanban board. Its mood is *quiet confidence*: deliberately low-chrome and low-anxiety, so that a busy professional opening the app feels the day get smaller rather than larger. The visual language is built on three pillars — **clarity, momentum, and restraint**. Clarity means one dominant thing per screen: the ranked "Today" queue (F-1) is a single vertical spine of tasks, never a grid of competing panels; the capture surface (F-2) is a single line floating above everything, never a form. Momentum means the interface always shows forward motion — tasks visibly rise, complete, and fall away with soft, short transitions, and a Focus session (F-3) collapses the entire product down to one task, one timer, one exit. Restraint means color is spent, not sprayed: a near-neutral canvas with a single confident accent reserved for the thing that matters right now (top-ranked task, active timer, primary action), while everything else is expressed through weight, spacing, and hierarchy rather than hue.

Visually the system is **typographic first and chromatic second**. A generous type scale does the heavy lifting: task titles are the largest, most legible element in the app; metadata (due time, effort, tags, rank explanation) is consistently smaller, lower-contrast, and never competes with the title. Spacing is spacious on the queue and tight inside dense analytical surfaces (F-4), so that "calm" and "information-rich" coexist without contradiction. Surfaces are layered rather than bordered — a soft, shallow elevation model communicates what is background, what is card, and what is an overlay, keeping the app free of a heavy box-and-line grid. Iconography is a single line-weight family, used sparingly and always paired with a label the first time it appears; nothing important is conveyed by icon or color alone.

Color is defined as **semantic roles, not fixed values** — canvas, surface, elevated surface, primary text, secondary text, hairline, accent, and a small set of state colors (success/complete, warning/at-risk, danger/overdue, info) plus connection health states for the Integration Hub (F-5: `connected`, `degraded`, `expired`, `error`, `paused`, `disconnected`). Because theming is a first-class product feature (F-6), every role must resolve to a legible value in both light and dark, and the dark theme must be designed as its own considered palette — deeper, desaturated surfaces with slightly warmed accents — not an inversion of light. No surface, chart series, or state token may rely on a value that only works in one theme, and every pairing must meet the accessibility contrast targets in §3.2. Priority is expressed through **position, weight, and a restrained accent bar**, never through a rainbow of severity colors — the ranking (F-1) should be readable at a glance from the shape of the list alone.

Motion is **short, purposeful, and reversible**: 120–200 ms for state changes, ease-out on entry, and no animation that delays a user from acting. Rank reorderings animate so the user can follow what moved and why; the ranking explanation (F-1) expands inline rather than hijacking the screen. Focus Mode (F-3) is the one place the product is allowed to feel cinematic — a dimmed periphery and a single elevated timer — and, correspondingly, the one place where exiting must always be one obvious, unmissable action. Analytics (F-4) prefers one honest series over a dashboard of competing charts: a small number of well-labeled visualizations, with the underlying numbers always readable as text, and never a decorative chart that cannot be explained in words.

The overall posture toward the user is **non-judgmental mentorship**: the app nudges (streaks, at-risk flags, suggested next task) but never scolds, gamifies aggressively, or reddens a screen. Empty and error states are written in the same voice — plain, warm, actionable — and the design direction treats "nothing here yet" as a first-class, attractive screen rather than an absence to be patched with a spinner.

## Components

The component system is layered in four tiers so that no feature (F-1 … F-6) re-implements shared behaviour. Naming is by noun-role only — **no framework, library, vendor, or rendering technology is implied by any component name**; technology binding remains the Architect's decision.

| Tier | Contents | Product knowledge |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Primitives | Tokens + atoms | none |
| 2. Composed components | Reusable compounds | product-aware, feature-agnostic |
| 3. Feature components | Bound to exactly one feature (F-n) | feature-specific |
| 4. Surfaces | Screens / overlays assembled from tiers 1–3 | screen-specific |

**Universal contract.** Every component, in every tier, is *theme-aware* (consumes F-6 tokens, FR-126 … FR-129) and *state-complete*: each declares **default / hover / focus-visible / active / disabled / loading / empty / error** variants. No component ships without its empty, loading, and error state.

---

### 4. Cross-feature composition rules

- **One dominant thing per surface.** `TodayQueue` (F-1) is the spine of the home surface; `QuickAddInput` (F-2) floats above it as the only overlay line; `FocusShell` (F-3) temporarily *replaces* the spine entirely.
- **Focus Mode suspends but never destroys context.** While `FocusShell` is active, F-1 / F-2 / F-4 surfaces are retained and restored on exit; `ActiveSessionIndicator` stays visible outside `FocusShell`.
- **Theming wraps everything.** `ThemeProvider` (F-6) is the outermost provider; every component consumes theme tokens, so no feature ships a hard-coded colour.
- **Integration states are ambient, never modal.** F-5 `degraded` / `expired` states surface via `StatusBanner` and per-row `ConnectionStateBadge` inside F-1 / F-2 — never as blocking dialogs.
- **Capture is always reachable.** `AppShell` mounts `CaptureBarHost` on every primary screen (FR-26). Inside `FocusShell` the bar is hidden to honour "one dominant thing" and restored on exit.
- **State completeness is mandatory.** Each component declares default / hover / focus-visible / active / disabled / loading / empty / error plus its theme-resolved token set.
