### 5. Component → feature traceability

| Component group | Feature | Representative global ids |
|---|---|---|
| Primitives (theme tokens) | all / F-6 | FR-126 … FR-129 |
| `AppShell`, `CaptureBarHost`, `PrimaryNavigation` | all / F-2 | FR-26 |
| F-1 group | F-1 | FR-1 … FR-9 |
| F-2 group | F-2 | FR-26 … FR-30 |
| F-3 group | F-3 | FR-51 … FR-56 |
| F-4 group | F-4 | FR-76 … FR-80 |
| F-5 group | F-5 | FR-101 … FR-103 |
| F-6 group | F-6 | FR-126 … FR-129 |

Local component ids are scoped within their owning feature and numbered sequentially from 1 (BR-, EC-, AC-, API-, DM-, T-, OQ-, V-); they are not re-declared here.

## Data Models

> Scope: logical, technology-neutral modelling. Storage engine, indexing strategy, physical schema, transport and secret custody are the Architect's decision. No framework, database, vendor or protocol is implied by any name below. Every model is owned by one or more features (`F-1` … `F-6`) and exists to satisfy the already-defined FR/NFR/US/API ranges for those features. Model ids `DM-1` … `DM-24` are defined here once and referenced elsewhere as plain text.

### 0. Modelling conventions

| # | Convention | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Identity | Every entity carries an immutable, opaque, globally unique `id`. Ids are never reused after deletion and are safe to mint on a client before server confirmation, so offline capture (F-2) never blocks or loses a task. |
| 2 | Ownership | Every user-owned entity carries `ownerId`. All reads and writes are scoped to the authenticated owner; no cross-owner reference is valid. |
| 3 | Time | All instants are stored in UTC at millisecond precision. User-facing calendar dates are always derived using the `timezoneId` recorded on `DM-22` at the moment of the event, and the timezone used is persisted alongside any rollup. |
| 4 | Soft delete | User-visible entities carry `deletedAt`. Deletion is reversible for a bounded grace period, then physically purged. Deletion never cascades silently across an integration boundary (see `DM-18`). |
| 5 | Concurrency | Every mutable entity carries a monotonic `version`. A write against a stale `version` is rejected rather than silently merged. |
| 6 | Derivation | Anything computable — priority score, queue rank, activity rollups, streaks, connection health — is a **derived entity** that can always be recomputed from source entities. Derived stores are caches, never sources of truth. |
| 7 | Enum discipline | Enumerations are closed sets. Unrecognized values arriving from an external system (F-5) map to an `unknown` member instead of being rejected, so one malformed payload cannot fail a whole sync. |
| 8 | Secret isolation | No credential, token, or signing secret is ever stored on a functional entity, emitted in a response, or written to an audit entry. Secrets are referenced only by an opaque handle (`DM-16`). |
| 9 | Provenance | Any value that can originate from a human, a parser, or an external system records its origin. This is what makes two-way sync conflicts and "why did this change?" answerable. |

### 2. Core entities

#### DM-1 — Task

The single source of truth for a unit of work. Every other feature reads or writes it; no feature keeps a private copy of a task.

| Field | Type (logical) | Req | Rules / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | Immutable, never reused. |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | Immutable after creation. |
| `title` | string, 1–500 after trim | yes | Non-empty after trimming. Long input is truncated for display, never silently lost. |
| `notes` | text | no | Free-form; not parsed. |
| `status` | enum `active \| completed \| canceled \| archived` | yes | Default `active`. See transition invariant below. |
| `createdAt` | timestamp (UTC) | yes | Server-assigned; also the anchor for the "task age" factor (FR-3). |
| `updatedAt` | timestamp (UTC) | yes | Any field change updates it. |
| `dueAt` | timestamp (UTC) \| null | no | Null means "no deadline". Consumed by the due-date factor and by urgency escalation (FR-3, FR-9). |
| `dueHasTime` | boolean | yes (default false) | Distinguishes "due 5 March" from "due 5 March 14:00" so a date-only deadline is never rendered as a late-evening time. Only meaningful when `dueAt` is set. |
| `importance` | integer 0–100 \| null | no | Explicit user importance. Null means "not stated" and must be treated as neutral by scoring, not as zero (FR-3, FR-28). |
| `importanceOrigin` | enum `user \| parsed \| integration \| default` | yes | Provenance of `importance` (convention 9). |
| `effortEstimateMinutes` | integer ≥ 1 \| null | no | Estimated effort. Null is neutral, not zero (FR-3). |
| `projectId` | ref → `DM-4` \| null | no | Null resolves to the owner's default project. |
| `dependencyState` | enum `none \| ready \| blocked` | derived | Computed from `DM-5`. Never written directly. |
| `origin` | enum `manual \| quick_add \| integration \| recurring` | yes | Provenance. `quick_add` links to `DM-9`; `integration` implies at least one `DM-18` link. |
| `captureAttemptId` | ref → `DM-9` \| null | no | Present when the task was created through the capture surface. |
| `completionOrigin` | enum `manual \| focus_session \| integration` \| null | no | Set when `status` becomes `completed`; distinguishes a user tick from an externally observed completion (relevant to F-4 metrics). |
| `completedAt` | timestamp (UTC) \| null | no | Set iff `status = completed`. |
| `canceledAt` / `archivedAt` | timestamp (UTC) \| null | no | Set iff the matching status is active. |
| `deletedAt` | timestamp (UTC) \| null | no | Soft delete. |
| `version` | integer, monotonic | yes | Optimistic concurrency (convention 5). |

**Invariants**

1. `completedAt` is non-null **iff** `status = completed`; `canceledAt` is non-null **iff** `status = canceled`; `archivedAt` is non-null **iff** `status = archived`.
2. Allowed status transitions: `active → completed`, `active → canceled`, `active → archived`, `completed → active` (reopen), `canceled → active` (restore), `archived → active` (restore). `completed → canceled` is not allowed — reopen first.
3. `dueHasTime` may only be true when `dueAt` is set.
4. A task with `deletedAt` set is excluded from the Today queue, from all metrics (F-4), and from any outgoing sync write (F-5), but its links (`DM-18`) are retained in an orphaned state so a re-import does not resurrect a deleted task silently.
5. `title` is never empty: a capture that parses to an empty title (see `DM-9`) must fail visibly before a task is created.

#### DM-2 — Tag

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | — |
| `label` | string 1–50 | yes | Display form, preserves user casing. |
| `normalizedLabel` | string | yes | Case-folded and whitespace-collapsed; uniqueness is enforced on this field. |
| `colorToken` | enum token name | no | A **theme token**, not a raw colour value, so tags re-theme correctly under F-6 (FR-129). |
| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `archivedAt` | timestamp \| null | no | Archived tags stay attached to history but are not offered for new tasks. |
| `usageCount` | integer | derived | Recomputed from `DM-3`. |

Uniqueness: one tag per `(ownerId, normalizedLabel)`.

#### DM-3 — TaskTagLink

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | Must equal the owner of both ends. |
| `taskId` | ref → `DM-1` | yes | Deleting the task removes its links. |
| `tagId` | ref → `DM-2` | yes | Deleting the tag removes its links. |
| `createdAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `origin` | enum `user \| parsed \| integration` | yes | Provenance (convention 9). |

Uniqueness: one row per `(taskId, tagId)`.

#### DM-4 — Project

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | — |
| `name` | string 1–100 | yes | — |
| `normalizedName` | string | yes | Uniqueness enforced here. |
| `isDefault` | boolean | yes | Exactly one default project per owner ("Inbox"); it cannot be deleted or archived. |
| `sortKey` | string | no | User-controlled ordering. |
| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `archivedAt` | timestamp \| null | no | Archiving re-homes its tasks to the default project; it never deletes them. |

#### DM-5 — TaskDependency

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | Both tasks must share this owner. |
| `blockedTaskId` | ref → `DM-1` | yes | The task that cannot proceed. |
| `blockingTaskId` | ref → `DM-1` | yes | The task that must finish first. |
| `createdAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `state` | enum `active \| satisfied \| invalidated` | derived | `satisfied` when the blocking task is `completed`; `invalidated` when either side was deleted or reopened after satisfaction. |

**Invariants**

1. No self-reference: `blockedTaskId ≠ blockingTaskId`.
2. The dependency graph is **acyclic**. Adding an edge that would create a cycle is rejected with an explanatory error, never silently dropped.
3. Duplicate edges are rejected: uniqueness on `(blockedTaskId, blockingTaskId)`.
4. Deleting the blocking task does not delete the edge; it flips the dependent task to `dependencyState = ready` and the edge to `invalidated`, so the ordering change is explainable (FR-5).
5. This entity feeds the dependency factor of `DM-7` directly; it is never duplicated into the task.

### 3. F-1 — Prioritization entities

#### DM-6 — PriorityProfile

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | One *active* profile per owner in the initial design (see OQ-1). |
| `revision` | integer, monotonic | yes | Increments on every weight change. |
| `weights` | list of `{ factor, weight }` | yes | `factor` ∈ `due_date`, `importance`, `effort`, `age`, `dependency` (the FR-3 minimum set). `weight` is a decimal 0–100. Weights are **relative**: scoring normalizes them, so any set of weights is valid. |
| `neutralPolicy` | map `factor → neutral value` | yes | Explicit declaration of what "no due date", "no effort estimate" and "no dependencies" contribute. Prevents a missing input from being scored as zero. |
| `isActive` | boolean | yes | Exactly one active profile per owner. |
| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `source` | enum `default \| user_tuned` | yes | Whether the user has ever edited weights (FR-4). |

**Invariants**

1. Every factor in the FR-3 minimum set is present in `weights`; a profile missing a factor is invalid.
2. `revision` never decreases; a rollback writes a new `revision` that reinstates old values, so history stays linear.
3. Profiles are versioned, not overwritten. `DM-7` references the `revision` it used, which is what makes an old ranking reproducible and an explanation truthful (FR-5).

#### DM-7 — PriorityScore (derived)

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `taskId` | ref → `DM-1` | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | — |
| `profileId` / `profileRevision` | ref + integer | yes | Exact inputs used. |
| `score` | decimal, normalized 0–100 | yes | Always defined: neutral policy (`DM-6`) guarantees every factor has a value. |
| `factorContributions` | list of `{ factor, rawInput, normalized 0–1, weight, contribution }` | yes | The substrate of the FR-5 explanation and of the weight editor's preview (FR-4). |
| `band` | enum `overdue \| due_today \| upcoming \| later \| undated \| blocked` | derived | Human-legible grouping used by the queue UI. |
| `rank` | integer ≥ 1 | derived | Position in the queue snapshot this score belongs to. |
| `queueScope` | enum `today \| project \| search` | yes | Rank is only meaningful inside its scope. |
| `explanationText` | text | derived | Plain-language rendering of the dominant factors (FR-5); regenerated from `factorContributions`, never hand-written. |
| `computedAt` / `expiresAt` | timestamp | yes | `expiresAt` drives the freshness expectation in NFR-5. |

**Invariants**

1. Derived and disposable: deleting all scores must leave the queue fully reconstructable.
2. Scores are monotonic in their inputs — increasing importance or nearing a deadline can never *lower* a task's score under a fixed profile revision.
3. A score is never used to compute another score; deep chains are forbidden so recomputation stays bounded.
4. `rank` is unique within `(queueScope, snapshot)` — two tasks never share a rank.

#### DM-8 — RankOverride

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` / `taskId` | refs | yes | — |
| `type` | enum `pin_top \| fixed_rank \| boost` | yes | `fixed_rank` requires `fixedRank`; the others must not set it. |
| `fixedRank` | integer ≥ 1 \| null | no | Required iff `type = fixed_rank`; may exceed the current queue length, in which case the task lands at the tail (recorded as an applied-with-adjustment event). |
| `createdAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `createdByDeviceId` | ref → `DM-23` | no | — |
| `expiresAt` | timestamp \| null | no | Time-boxed override (FR-7). |
| `expiresOnCompletion` | boolean | yes (default true) | Override auto-releases when the task completes (FR-7). |
| `reason` | string ≤ 200 | no | Optional note shown in the explanation. |
| `isActive` | boolean | yes | — |
| `releasedAt` | timestamp \| null | no | Set when released manually, by expiry, or by completion. |

**Invariants**

1. At most **one** active override per task; creating a second requires the first to be released explicitly (the UI must ask, not silently replace).
2. An override never modifies `DM-7.score` — it changes final ordering only. Removing an override must return the task to exactly the position its score implies, which is why scores are retained while an override is active.
3. Auto-release on expiry or completion is recorded in `DM-24` and surfaces as a transient, dismissible notice so the user sees the queue re-order (FR-8).
4. Overrides never expire while `isActive = true` and `expiresAt` is null (indefinite is a first-class choice).

### 4. F-2 — Quick Add entities

#### DM-9 — CaptureAttempt

Every capture creates a record, even one that is discarded, so parsing can be explained and improved and so an interrupted capture is recoverable.

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | Client-mintable so an offline capture is never lost (convention 1). |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | — |
| `deviceId` | ref → `DM-23` | no | — |
| `rawText` | string, 1–1000 | yes | The user's untouched input. |
| `capturedAt` | timestamp, client + server | yes | Both retained; the server timestamp is authoritative for ordering, the client timestamp preserves intent when the device was offline. |
| `timezoneAtCapture` | IANA string | yes | Relative expressions such as "tomorrow 5pm" are resolved with this zone, not the current one (see DM-22 invariant 2). |
| `parseResult` | structured | derived | `title`, `dueAt`, `dueHasTime`, `importance`, `importanceOrigin = parsed`, `tagTokens[]`, `projectToken`, `unrecognizedTokens[]`. |
| `parseConfidence` | map `field → decimal 0–1` | derived | Drives the preview and the "check this" affordance (FR-30). |
| `parserVersion` | string | yes | Provenance of the interpretation; a re-parse can be offered when the parser improves. |
| `status` | enum `parsed \| applied \| discarded \| superseded` | yes | `applied` implies exactly one `taskId`. |
| `taskId` | ref → `DM-1` \| null | no | Set iff `status = applied`. |
| `discardReason` | enum `user_cancelled \| empty_title \| duplicate \| error` \| null | no | — |

**Invariants**

1. Nothing that fails to parse is silently dropped: an unrecognized token stays in `title`, and its presence is visible in the preview (FR-29, FR-30).
2. A capture produces at most one task (FR-26 defines one line → one task); a second confirm while the first is in flight is deduplicated by `id`, not by creating two tasks.
3. `status = applied` requires a non-empty resolved `title`. A capture that resolves to an empty title is blocked pre-creation with an inline error, and the raw text remains editable.
4. Applying a capture is a single atomic step: task + tags + project link are created together or not at all.
5. `rawText` retention is bounded by the retention policy in §10 (see OQ-2).

### 5. F-3 — Focus Mode entities

#### DM-10 — FocusSession

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | — |
| `taskId` | ref → `DM-1` | yes | A session is always bound to one existing task (FR-51); unbound "just a timer" sessions are not modelled (see OQ-3). |
| `state` | enum `running \| paused \| completed \| abandoned \| expired` | yes | Single active session per owner (FR-55). |
| `plannedDurationMinutes` | integer 1–600 | yes | Initialized from `DM-22.defaultFocusDurationMinutes` (built-in default 25), overridable per session (FR-52, FR-53). |
| `extensionMinutesTotal` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | Sum of all extensions in this session (FR-54). |
| `startedAt` | timestamp | yes | Server clock is authoritative. |
| `lastResumedAt` | timestamp \| null | yes | Non-null iff `state = running`. |
| `endedAt` | timestamp \| null | no | Non-null iff `state ∈ {completed, abandoned, expired}`. |
| `effectiveDurationSeconds` | integer ≥ 0 | derived | Active time only; pauses excluded. Never exceeds wall-clock duration. |
| `accumulatedPauseSeconds` | integer ≥ 0 | derived | — |
| `pauseCount` / `interruptionCount` | integer ≥ 0 | derived | Interruption = pause followed by an out-of-app return, per FR-56's interruption reporting. |
| `outcome` | enum `target_reached \| stopped_early \| abandoned \| auto_expired` \| null | no | Non-null iff the session has ended. |
| `taskCompletedInSession` | boolean | yes (default false) | Set only by an explicit user action; ending a session never auto-completes the task. |
| `deviceId` | ref → `DM-23` | no | — |
| `version` | integer | yes | Optimistic concurrency (convention 5). |

**Invariants**

1. **At most one session per owner is in `running` or `paused` at any instant.** Enforced as a uniqueness constraint over the active states, not by UI alone.
2. `plannedDurationMinutes + extensionMinutesTotal` must stay within the supported range; an extension that would exceed it is rejected with a clear message rather than silently clamped.
3. `endedAt ≥ startedAt`; `effectiveDurationSeconds ≤ (endedAt − startedAt)`.
4. Deleting the bound task while a session is active does **not** silently kill the session — the session is preserved as an orphaned record and the user is asked whether to stop or re-bind (see §8, EC for F-3).
5. A session for a `completed` task may only be started as a fresh session; sessions are never retro-attached to a closed range.
6. Client/server clock disagreement is resolved in favour of the server, and the correction is recorded (see `DM-11`).

#### DM-11 — FocusSessionEvent

Append-only. The session's timeline must be reconstructable and reconcilable across devices.

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `sessionId` | ref → `DM-10` | yes | — |
| `type` | enum `started \| paused \| resumed \| extended \| ended \| abandoned \| auto_expired \| clock_corrected \| reconciled` | yes | — |
| `at` | timestamp, server | yes | — |
| `clientAt` | timestamp \| null | no | Retained when it differed from `at` by more than the tolerance, so a discrepancy is explainable. |
| `deltaMinutes` | integer \| null | no | Required for `extended`. |
| `actorDeviceId` | ref → `DM-23` | no | — |
| `note` | string | no | Free-form, non-secret. |

**Invariants**

1. Records are immutable; a correction is a new record, never an edit.
2. The ordered event list must be sufficient to recompute `effectiveDurationSeconds`, `pauseCount` and `outcome` from scratch.
3. Events for a session must form a valid state machine; an event that would produce an illegal transition is rejected. Duplicate deliveries of the same event (retry, dual device) are idempotent by `id`.

### 6. F-4 — Progress Analytics entities

#### DM-12 — ProgressPreference

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | Unique per owner. |
| `defaultPeriod` | enum `7d \| 30d \| 90d \| custom` | yes | Default `7d`. |
| `customRangeStart` / `customRangeEnd` | date (owner-local) \| null | no | Required iff `defaultPeriod = custom`; start ≤ end. |
| `weekStartDay` | enum `monday \| sunday \| saturday \| locale` | yes | Default `locale`, resolved via `DM-22`. |
| `streakDefinition` | enum `days_with_completion \| days_with_focus_session` | yes | Default `days_with_completion` (FR-80). |
| `metricVisibility` | map `metric → boolean` | yes | Which dashboard blocks are shown. |
| `lastViewedAt` | timestamp | no | — |
| `updatedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |

**Invariants**

1. Changing `streakDefinition` takes effect from the change date forward; historical `DM-14` rows keep their original definition and are not rewritten. Both facts are shown in the UI so the change is never mysterious.
2. Changing `weekStartDay` recomputes weekly series but never alters daily rollups.

#### DM-13 — DailyActivityRollup (derived)

One row per owner per **owner-local calendar date**.

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | — |
| `dateLocal` | date (owner-local) | yes | Uniqueness on `(ownerId, dateLocal)`. |
| `timezoneUsed` | IANA string | yes | The zone in force when the date was bucketed (convention 3). |
| `tasksCreated` | integer ≥ 0 | derived | From `DM-1.createdAt`. |
| `tasksCompleted` | integer ≥ 0 | derived | From `DM-1.completedAt` and `completionOrigin`. |
| `tasksCompletedViaFocus` | integer ≥ 0 | derived | Subset of the above; supports FR-77/FR-79 breakdowns. |
| `netChange` | integer | derived | `tasksCreated − tasksCompleted` (FR-77). |
| `completionRate` | decimal 0–100 \| null | derived | `tasksCompleted ÷ tasksCreated`; null when `tasksCreated = 0` — never rendered as 0 %, which would be a lie. |
| `focusMinutes` | integer ≥ 0 | derived | Sum of `DM-10.effectiveDurationSeconds ÷ 60` for sessions ending that date. |
| `focusSessionCount` | integer ≥ 0 | derived | — |
| `computedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `sourceWatermark` | timestamp | yes | Latest source `updatedAt` folded in; used to decide whether a recompute is needed. |

**Invariants**

1. Purely derived and fully recomputable; deleting the table must not change any number the user sees after recompute.
2. A late-arriving change (an external system reports a completion dated yesterday) triggers recompute of the affected dates only, and the dashboard shows a non-blocking "updated" indication rather than an unexplained jump.
3. Rollups never include deleted or canceled tasks as completions, but a task completed and later reopened removes one from the completion count of its original date.
4. There is no future-dated rollup; a zero-activity day exists implicitly and may be materialized on read.

#### DM-14 — StreakRecord (derived)

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | — |
| `kind` | enum `current \| longest` | yes | FR-80. |
| `definition` | enum mirroring `DM-12.streakDefinition` | yes | Historical rows keep the definition they were computed with. |
| `lengthDays` | integer ≥ 0 | derived | — |
| `startDateLocal` / `endDateLocal` | date | derived | Inclusive range. |
| `isProvisional` | boolean | derived | True for a `current` streak that includes today, since today can still break it. |
| `computedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |

**Invariants**

1. `longest.lengthDays` never decreases for a given definition.
2. A streak of length 0 is representable and is displayed as "no streak yet" with an encouraging empty state, not as a bare zero.
3. At most one `current` and one `longest` row per `(ownerId, definition)`.
4. A streak is continuous by local calendar date: a missed local day breaks it, and the timezone used for the boundary is the one recorded in `DM-13`.

### 7. F-5 — Integration Hub entities

#### DM-15 — Connection

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | — |
| `providerType` | enum `calendar \| email \| issue_tracker \| code_host \| messaging \| file_store \| generic_webhook` | yes | Mirrors the catalogue (FR-101). |
| `providerId` | string | yes | Which concrete provider within the type; opaque to the functional layer. |
| `label` | string 1–80 | yes | User-editable, defaults to the account display name. |
| `accountIdentityDisplay` | string | yes | Human-readable identity (e.g. an address or handle). Never a secret. |
| `state` | enum `connected \| degraded \| expired \| error \| paused \| disconnected` | yes | FR-103. |
| `scopesGranted` | list of scope strings | yes | What the user actually authorized; drives capability claims. |
| `capabilities` | map `dataType → { read, write }` | yes | What the catalogue promised **and** what the grant permits; if the two differ, the narrower one wins and the difference is surfaced. |
| `syncPolicy` | enum `auto \| manual` + `frequencyMinutes` | yes | Default `auto`; user-changeable. |
| `connectedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `lastSyncAt` | timestamp \| null | yes | Most recent attempt. |
| `lastSuccessfulSyncAt` | timestamp \| null | yes | Most recent success. |
| `consecutiveFailureCount` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | Drives `degraded` → `error` promotion. |
| `lastErrorCode` | enum | no | Machine-readable, so the UI can offer a specific recovery action. |
| `lastErrorMessage` | string | no | User-safe wording; never raw provider payloads, never credentials. |
| `pausedAt` / `disconnectedAt` | timestamp \| null | no | Set iff the matching state is active. |
| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `version` | integer | yes | — |

**Allowed state transitions (nothing else is valid):**

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| — | `connected` | Successful authorization callback (FR-102). A connection only appears after a successful callback; a partially completed handshake leaves no connection row. |
| `connected` | `degraded` | First transient sync failure. |
| `degraded` | `connected` | A sync succeeds. |
| `degraded` | `error` | Failures reach the escalation threshold. |
| `expired` | `connected` | Successful reauthorization. |
| `error` / `expired` / `degraded` | `paused` | Explicit user pause. |
| `paused` | `connected` | Explicit user resume, followed by a verification sync. |
| any connected-ish state | `disconnected` | Explicit user disconnection. |
| `disconnected` | `connected` | A fresh authorization handshake. |

**Invariants**

1. `paused` and `disconnected` both stop scheduled syncs, but `paused` preserves the authorization and queued actions, while `disconnected` revokes the secret reference and terminally fails queued actions with a stated reason.
2. Exactly one connection may exist per `(ownerId, providerType, accountIdentityDisplay)`; attempting a duplicate is reported as already connected with a link to the existing one, never as a silent second row.
3. No credential material lives on this entity (convention 8).

#### DM-16 — ConnectionSecretRef

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `connectionId` | ref → `DM-15` | yes | — |
| `purpose` | enum `access_token \| refresh_token \| webhook_signing_secret \| client_secret` | yes | — |
| `handle` | opaque string | yes | Reference into whatever custody mechanism the Architect selects. The handle is meaningless outside the app and is never returned to a client. |
| `issuedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `expiresAt` | timestamp \| null | no | — |
| `lastRefreshedAt` | timestamp \| null | no | — |
| `rotationGeneration` | integer ≥ 1 | yes | Increments on rotation so an in-flight action can be attributed to the generation that authorized it. |
| `status` | enum `active \| expired \| revoked` | yes | — |

**Invariants**

1. No entity, response, log line or audit entry anywhere in the system contains secret material; only handles do.
2. Revocation is immediate and idempotent, and is recorded in `DM-24`. Marking a `DM-15` as `disconnected` revokes all of its handles.
3. Exactly one `active` handle per `(connectionId, purpose)`.

#### DM-17 — SyncRun

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `connectionId` | ref → `DM-15` | yes | — |
| `direction` | enum `inbound \| outbound \| bidirectional` | yes | — |
| `trigger` | enum `scheduled \| manual \| webhook \| retry` | yes | — |
| `state` | enum `running \| succeeded \| partially_succeeded \| failed \| rate_limited \| canceled` | yes | — |
| `startedAt` / `finishedAt` | timestamp | yes / nullable | `finishedAt` null iff `state = running`. |
| `counters` | map | derived | `itemsRead`, `created`, `updated`, `skipped`, `conflicted`, `failed`. |
| `errorSummary` | string | no | User-safe. Never raw provider payloads. |
| `cursorBefore` / `cursorAfter` | opaque string \| null | no | Enables incremental sync without re-reading everything. Only advanced on success or partial success. |
| `retryOf` | ref → `DM-17` \| null | no | — |
| `nextRetryAt` | timestamp \| null | no | Exponential backoff; cleared on success. |

**Invariants**

1. At most one `running` run per `(connectionId, direction)`; a second trigger while one is running is coalesced and reported as "already syncing", not queued blindly.
2. Failure isolation: an individual item that cannot be applied increments `failed` and the run continues. A healthy run reports `partially_succeeded`, never a binary success/failure that hides which items were affected.
3. `cursorAfter` is never advanced past items that failed, so the next run retries them.
4. Every terminal run writes exactly one user-visible health update on `DM-15`.

#### DM-18 — ExternalItemLink

The join between a local task and the external item it mirrors, plus the field-ownership map that makes two-way sync predictable.

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `connectionId` | ref → `DM-15` | yes | — |
| `externalId` | string | yes | Uniqueness on `(connectionId, externalId, externalType)`. |
| `externalType` | enum mapped from the provider's item kinds | yes | Unknown kinds map to `unknown` (convention 7). |
| `taskId` | ref → `DM-1` \| null | no | Null when the item is `ignored` or was `orphaned` by a local deletion. |
| `linkState` | enum `linked \| ignored \| orphaned \| unlinked` | yes | — |
| `externalVersion` | string \| null | no | ETag / revision / `updatedAt` from the provider, used for conflict detection. |
| `fieldOwnership` | map `field → local \| external \| newest_wins` | yes | Explicit per field: title, dueAt, importance, status, project, tags. This is the whole conflict rule; it is never implicit. |
| `firstSeenAt` / `lastSeenAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `lastSyncedAt` | timestamp \| null | no | — |
| `lastConflict` | structured \| null | no | `{ field, localValue, externalValue, resolvedBy, resolvedAt }` — retained so a surprising value is explainable. |

**Invariants**

1. A task may be linked to several external items across connections; a local field is only overwritten by an external value if that field's ownership rule permits it.
2. `orphaned` is never a silent delete: a locally deleted task leaves its link, and a later re-import of the same external item does not resurrect the task without explicit user action.
3Because external identities are the join key, storing them is mandatory before any external write is attempted — that is what makes write-back idempotent.

#### DM-19 — IntegrationAction

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `connectionId` | ref → `DM-15` | yes | — |
| `taskId` | ref → `DM-1` \| null | no | Null for non-task actions (e.g. posting a message). |
| `externalItemLinkId` | ref → `DM-18` \| null | no | Required for `update`/`complete`/`delete`; null for `create` until the external id is known. |
| `actionType` | enum `create \| update \| complete \| delete \| comment \| notify` | yes | Must be permitted by `DM-15.capabilities.write`. |
| `payloadSummary` | structured, non-secret | yes | Enough to explain the action in an activity list; never a full payload dump, never a credential. |
| `requestedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `requestedBy` | enum `user \| automation \| integration` + actor ref | yes | — |
| `state` | enum `queued \| in_flight \| succeeded \| failed \| retrying \| dead_letter \| canceled` | yes | — |
| `attemptCount` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | — |
| `lastAttemptAt` | timestamp \| null | no | — |
| `lastErrorCode` / `lastErrorMessage` | enum / string | no | User-safe. |
| `idempotencyKey` | string | yes | Unique per `(connectionId, idempotencyKey)`. |
| `resultExternalVersion` | string \| null | no | Written back to `DM-18.externalVersion` on success. |
| `nextRetryAt` | timestamp \| null | no | — |

**Invariants**

1. Retrying an action must never duplicate the external write; `idempotencyKey` is the guarantee (convention on at-least-once delivery).
2. Actions queued while a connection is `paused` remain `queued` and are not silently dropped; they resume when it is resumed, and are terminally failed with a stated reason when it is `disconnected`.
3. An action the connection is not authorized to perform is rejected at enqueue time with a clear capability message, not failed later after the user believes it worked.
4. `dead_letter` is terminal and must be surfaced to the user with a retry option — never swallowed.
5. Any action that changes local state optimistically carries the originating task `version`, so a stale action cannot clobber a newer local edit.

#### DM-20 — WebhookDelivery

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `connectionId` | ref → `DM-15` | yes | — |
| `eventId` | string | yes | Uniqueness per connection; the dedupe key for at-least-once delivery. |
| `eventType` | string | yes | — |
| `signatureKeyRef` | ref → `DM-16` | no | Reference only; the signing secret value is never stored here. |
| `attemptedAt` | timestamp | yes | Append-only per attempt. |
| `attemptCount` | integer ≥ 1 | yes | — |
| `responseStatusClass` | enum `2xx \| 3xx \| 4xx \| 5xx \| timeout \| network_error` \| null | no | — |
| `state` | enum `pending \| delivered \| failed \| dead_letter` | yes | — |
| `nextAttemptAt` | timestamp \| null | no | — |
| `payloadFingerprint` | string | yes | Proves what was sent without storing the whole payload. |

**Invariants**

1. Exactly one terminal state per `(eventId, connectionId)`; retries update the same logical delivery rather than creating duplicates for the receiver.
2. A `4xx` other than a rate-limit code is terminal (`dead_letter`) — retrying a rejected request forever is forbidden.
3. Delivery records are append-only and never contain secrets or full user content beyond the fingerprint.

### 8. F-6 — Dark Mode entity

#### DM-21 — ThemePreference

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | — |
| `deviceId` | ref → `DM-23` \| null | no | Null row = the account-level default; per-device rows override it (FR-128). |
| `preference` | enum `light \| dark \| system` | yes | The user's **choice**, and the only value a user can set (FR-126). Exactly one of the three; no per-screen or per-widget value exists anywhere in the model. |
| `effectiveTheme` | enum `light \| dark` | derived | The concrete theme actually rendered. |
| `resolvedFrom` | enum `user_choice \| system_signal \| account_default \| built_in_default` | derived | Makes an unexpected theme explainable. |
| `lastSystemSignal` | enum `light \| dark \| unknown` | derived | Last observed OS/browser signal (FR-127). |
| `updatedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `revision` | integer, monotonic | yes | Bumped on every change; lets a client detect a stale preference. |

**Invariants**

1. Exactly one preference row per `(ownerId, deviceId)` and exactly one per `ownerId` with `deviceId = null`.
21. Exactly one preference row per `(ownerId, deviceId)` and exactly one per `ownerId` with `deviceId = null`.
2. The user's **choice** is never overwritten by the system signal. Flipping the OS between light and dark while `preference = system` changes only `effectiveTheme` and `lastSystemSignal`; `preference` stays `system` (FR-127).
3. An `unknown` system signal must still resolve to a concrete `effectiveTheme` through the fallback chain `account_default → built_in_default`. An unresolvable theme is not a representable state, because an unthemed flash is a visible defect (FR-129).
4. Preference application is local-first: a client may render from its own persisted value before any server round trip, then reconcile using `revision`. A stale-but-valid theme is always preferable to a flash of the wrong theme.
5. On sign-in, an existing per-device row for that device takes precedence over the account default; the account default applies only where no per-device row exists. Sign-out deletes neither row (FR-128).
6. There is no entity anywhere in the model that stores a per-screen, per-widget, or per-component theme value. Such a value cannot be expressed, so it cannot be introduced by accident.

### 9. Platform entities

#### DM-22 — UserProfile

The owner root. Every other user-owned entity resolves its scope through this row.

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | Also the `ownerId` referenced by every other entity. |
| `displayName` | string 1–120 | yes | — |
| `timezoneId` | IANA string | yes | **The** authority for every local-date derivation in the product (convention 3). |
| `locale` | BCP-47 string | yes | Drives date, time, number and currency formatting (NFR-16 range consumers). |
| `defaultFocusDurationMinutes` | integer 1–600 | yes | Built-in default 25. Used only to initialize a **new** session (FR-52). |
| `focusDurationPresets` | list of integers 1–600, ≤ 6 entries | no | Quick choices offered before a session starts (FR-53). |
| `defaultPriorityProfileId` | ref → `DM-6` | yes | Exactly one active profile (FR-4). |
| `defaultProjectId` | ref → `DM-4` | yes | The "Inbox" project; must exist before any task is created (DM-1 invariant 5). |
| `streakDefinitionDefault` | enum mirroring `DM-12.streakDefinition` | yes | Seeds a new `DM-12` row (FR-80). |
| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `deletedAt` | timestamp \| null | no | Account-level deletion; cascades per §11. |
| `version` | integer | yes | — |

**Invariants**

1. Exactly one `DM-22` per owner, created atomically with the default project and the default priority profile — the system never has a state in which a user exists without both.
2. Changing `timezoneId` does **not** rewrite historical `DM-13` or `DM-14` rows. Those keep the `timezoneUsed` they were computed with, and the dashboard states the zone boundary it used so a changed number is explainable (convention 3).
3. Changing `defaultFocusDurationMinutes` never mutates a `DM-10` row that is already `running` or `paused` (FR-52 applies to new sessions only).
4. `defaultPriorityProfileId` must reference a profile whose `isActive = true`; deactivating a profile requires another to be nominated in the same operation (DM-6 invariant 1).

#### DM-23 — Device

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | Client-minted on first launch; stable for the install. |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` \| null | no | Null while unauthenticated. |
| `label` | string 1–80 | yes | User-visible name; defaults to a platform-derived label. |
| `platformClass` | enum `desktop \| tablet \| phone \| unknown` | yes | Used for layout expectations only; never for authorization. |
| `firstSeenAt` / `lastSeenAt` | timestamp | yes | — |
| `clientVersion` | string | no | Diagnostic only; never used to gate behaviour. |
| `clockSkewSeconds` | integer | derived | Last observed difference from server time; drives the `clock_corrected` event (see `DM-11`). |
| `revokedAt` | timestamp \| null | no | Set when a user revokes a device. |
| `createdAt` / `updatedAt` | timestamp | yes | — |

**Invariants**

1. A device row is never hard-deleted while referenced by `DM-10`, `DM-11`, `DM-19`, `DM-21` or `DM-24`; revocation sets `revokedAt` and severs future writes, leaving history intact.
2. A revoked device may still read nothing; its queued `DM-19` actions are terminal-failed with a stated reason rather than silently dropped.
3. `clockSkewSeconds` beyond tolerance makes the server clock authoritative for all timing writes (F-3 sessions, F-1 urgency, F-2 relative dates) and the correction is recorded, so the user is never told a session ran for a duration the records contradict.

#### DM-24 — AuditEvent

Append-only history. This is what makes the explainability and reversibility requirements answerable after the fact, and what lets a user see that an override expired rather than silently vanishing.

| Field | Type | Req | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `ownerId` | ref → `DM-22` | yes | — |
| `at` | timestamp, server | yes | Client `at` retained separately when it differed. |
| `actorType` | enum `user \| system \| integration \| automation` | yes | — |
| `actorDeviceId` | ref → `DM-23` \| null | no | Present for `user` actors. |
| `eventType` | closed enum (below) | yes | An unrecognized event type is not representable; new behaviour requires a deliberate extension. |
| `subjectType` | enum `task \| tag \| project \| dependency \| priority_profile \| rank_override \| capture \| focus_session \| connection \| integration_action \| webhook_delivery \| theme_preference \| user_profile \| export \| purge` | yes | — |
| `subjectId` | opaque id | yes | — |
| `beforeSummary` / `afterSummary` | structured, non-secret \| null | no | Redacted to field names and safe values; never raw payloads, never credentials. |
| `reason` | enum `user_action \| expiry \| completion \| policy \| provider_change \| reconciliation \| retention` \| null | no | — |
| `correlationId` | string \| null | no | Groups one user action that touched several entities. |
| `retentionClass` | enum `standard \| extended \| until_account_deletion` | yes | Drives the purge matrix in §12. |

**Required event types (minimum closed set)**

`task.created` · `task.updated` · `task.status_changed` · `task.deleted` · `task.restored` · `task.bulk_reordered` · `dependency.added` · `dependency.rejected_cycle` · `dependency.invalidated` · `priority_profile.updated` · `priority_profile.rollback` · `rank_override.created` · `rank_override.released` · `rank_override.adjusted` · `capture.applied` · `capture.discarded` · `focus_session.started` · `focus_session.paused` · `focus_session.extended` · `focus_session.ended` · `focus_session.abandoned` · `focus_session.auto_expired` · `focus_session.clock_corrected` · `streak_definition.changed` · `period.changed` · `connection.authorized` · `connection.state_changed` · `connection.secret_rotated` · `connection.secret_revoked` · `integration_action.enqueued` · `integration_action.failed` · `integration_action.dead_lettered` · `integration_item.orphaned` · `integration_item.reconciled` · `webhook.delivery_failed` · `theme.preference_changed` · `theme.resolved_from_signal` · `data.exported` · `data.purged`.

**Invariants**

1. Append-only. A correction is a new event; no event is ever edited or deleted except by an accounted retention purge (`reason = retention`), which itself emits `data.purged`.
2. **No secrets, ever.** `beforeSummary`/`afterSummary` may name a field and say "changed", but may not carry a token, a signing secret, a raw provider payload, or a full captured line of user text (convention 8).
3. Every requirement in this spec that promises the user an explanation (F-1 FR-5, FR-8) or a visible consequence of an automatic change (F-5 FR-103, F-3 FR-56) has at least one corresponding event type above. An automatic state change with no event type is a modelling bug.
4. Volume is bounded: events carry summaries, not snapshots. An event must not grow with the size of the entity it describes.
5. Correlated events share a `correlationId`, so one user action that touched four entities reads as one story rather than four unrelated entries.

### 10. Cross-entity integrity

#### 10.1 Reference and deletion matrix

| Deleting | Effect on references |
|---|---|
| `DM-1` Task | Removes its `DM-3` links and its `DM-7` score; deactivates its `DM-8` overrides and records them as released; `DM-5` edges touching it flip to `invalidated` and the counterpart becomes `dependencyState = ready`; `DM-9` capture keeps `taskId` but is marked `superseded`; `DM-18` links become `orphaned` (**not** deleted); `DM-10` sessions are preserved as orphaned history and their `outcome` is back-filled; `DM-13`/`DM-14` are recomputed for the affected dates; `DM-19` queued actions for it are canceled with a stated reason. |
| `DM-2` Tag | Removes its `DM-3` links; `usageCount` recomputed. Tasks are untouched. |
| `DM-4` Project | Its tasks re-home to the default project (`DM-22.defaultProjectId`) in one atomic step; the default project itself cannot be removed. |
| `DM-5` Dependency edge | Only the edge is removed; neither task changes `status`. |
| `DM-6` PriorityProfile | Cannot be removed while active; superseding requires a new revision. `DM-7` rows keep their `profileRevision` and remain interpretable. |
| `DM-8` RankOverride | Releasing it must restore the task to the position its `DM-7.score` implies — the score is deliberately retained while an override is active so this is exact. |
| `DM-9` CaptureAttempt | Purged only by retention; never removed on task deletion. |
| `DM-10` FocusSession | Not deletable by the user. Purged only with the account or by retention; `DM-11` events are removed in the same transaction. |
| `DM-15` Connection | Queued `DM-19` actions terminal-fail with a stated reason; `DM-16` handles are revoked; `DM-18` links become `unlinked` with `taskId` preserved so the local task survives a disconnection intact (disconnecting must never destroy the user's tasks). |
| `DM-16` SecretRef | Revoking is idempotent and immediate; in-flight `DM-19` actions fail attribution and are retried under the next `rotationGeneration` or fail with a clear message. |
| `DM-18` ExternalItemLink | The local `DM-1` task is never deleted as a consequence. |
| `DM-22` UserProfile | Account deletion cascades per §12 with a stated grace period, and emits a terminal purge record. |
| `DM-23` Device | Never hard-deleted while referenced (see DM-23 invariant 1). |

#### 10.2 Consistency units

| Unit | Atomic boundary | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Capture apply | `DM-9` status change + `DM-1` creation + `DM-3` links + project assignment | A capture must never leave a half-created task visible (DM-9 invariant 4). |
| Completion | `DM-1.status` + `completedAt` + `completionOrigin` + affected `DM-13`/`DM-14` recompute + `DM-8` auto-release + `DM-24` event | Removes the window where the tick is visible but the metrics have not moved (F-4). |
| Queue recompute | `DM-6` weight change + `DM-7` invalidation + re-rank + `DM-24` event | Prevents a queue that visibly disagrees with the weights the user just saved (FR-4). |
| Focus state change | `DM-10.state` + `DM-11` event + single-active-session constraint check | The single-active-session rule is enforced in the same transaction as the state write, not by UI (DM-10 invariant 1). |
| Connection state change | `DM-15.state` + `DM-16` handle status + `DM-19` queue effects + `DM-24` event | A disconnected connection must not leave a live token or a live queue. |
| Theme change | `DM-21` row write + `revision` bump; rendering does not wait on it | Local-first application with server reconciliation (DM-21 invariant 4). |

### 11. Derived-data lifecycle

| Derived set | Invalidation triggers | Recompute scope | User-visible staleness contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DM-7` PriorityScore | task created/updated/completed/deleted; any `DM-5` edge change; `DM-6` revision bump; local-date rollover under `DM-22.timezoneId` (a "due today" task must become due today at the owner's midnight, not the server's) | The affected task; whole queue only on a profile or rollover change | Recompute is not allowed to block the UI. A queue may render from a stale score for at most the freshness window in the NFR-5 range, then must show an updating indicator (NFR-4 range). |
| `DM-13` DailyActivityRollup | completion, reopen, task deletion, `completionOrigin` change, focus session ended, timezone change (from the change point forward only) | Only the affected local dates, using `sourceWatermark` | A late-arriving external completion updates the affected day and surfaces a non-blocking "updated" cue rather than an unexplained jump (DM-13 invariant 2). |
| `DM-14` StreakRecord | any change to a relevant `DM-13` date; `streakDefinition` change | Current streak always; longest only when the current exceeds it | `isProvisional = true` while today can still break the streak, so a streak is never shown as final before the local day ends (DM-14 invariant 4). |
| `DM-1.dependencyState` | `DM-5` edge created/invalidated/satisfied | The single affected task | Never stale: it is computed on read of the queue, so a "blocked" badge cannot linger after its blocker completes. |
| `DM-2.usageCount` | `DM-3` link added/removed | The single tag | Tolerated staleness; never used for correctness. |
| `DM-15` health fields | every terminal `DM-17` run | The single connection | Health is pushed, not polled, so the connection list cannot show `connected` for a connection that a sync has already proven broken. |
| `DM-21.effectiveTheme` | preference change; system signal change; account default change; new device with no row | The single device, resolved locally first | Must resolve with **no** network dependency (DM-21 invariant 3, 4). |

**Invariant for the whole section:** dropping every derived entity and recomputing from sources must produce byte-identical user-visible numbers and orderings. If it does not, the derivation is under-specified — that is the test for whether a derived model is legitimate.

### 12. Retention and purge

| Data | Retention | Purge trigger | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DM-1` soft-deleted task | Grace period fixed by policy (see OQ-5) | Grace elapsed, or account deletion | Restorable during grace (DM-1 invariant 2); `DM-24` records both delete and restore. |
| `DM-9.rawText` | Bounded window (see OQ-6) | Retention elapsed | Free text is the most sensitive capture data; after purge the applied `DM-1` task is untouched and the parse is still explainable from `parseResult`. |
| `DM-10` / `DM-11` | Until account deletion | Account deletion | Sessions feed analytics; shortening this would silently change F-4 history. |
| `DM-13` / `DM-14` | Until account deletion | Account deletion | Recomputable from `DM-1`, but retained so a purge of tasks cannot retroactively rewrite the metrics the user saw. |
| `DM-16` revoked handle | Metadata until account deletion; secret material revoked immediately | — | The handle is retained only so an audit trail can say *that* a rotation happened (DM-16 invariant 2). |
| `DM-17` / `DM-19` / `DM-20` | Rolling window sized by `retentionClass` | Retention elapsed | Terminal failures (`dead_letter`) are retained longer than successes so a user-reported failure is still diagnosable. |
| `DM-18` `orphaned`/`unlinked` links | Until account deletion | Account deletion | Retained deliberately so a re-import cannot silently resurrect a deleted task (DM-18 invariant 2). |
| `DM-24` by `retentionClass` | `standard` < `extended` < `until_account_deletion` | Retention elapsed for that class | Purging emits its own `data.purged` event; an unexplained gap in the audit trail is not permissible. |

### 14. Modelling constraints and non-goals

1. **Single-owner by construction.** Every scoped entity carries `ownerId` and no model expresses sharing, membership, or cross-owner visibility. Adding collaboration later is a deliberate extension, not an accident of a missing column (see OQ-7).
2. **No vendor, engine, index, partition or replication concept appears above.** Physical shape, indexing for the queue read path, and secret custody are the Architect's decisions. The only storage obligations this model imposes are the invariants: uniqueness rules, the single-active-session constraint, append-only histories, idempotency keys, and monotonic versions.
3. **No denormalized copy of a task outside `DM-1`.** The queue, analytics and integrations all read the same row, so a completion in one place is a completion everywhere.
4. **Every timestamp is UTC; every local date is derived, never stored raw** except in `DM-13`/`DM-14`, where the derivation is frozen deliberately and the timezone used is recorded beside it.
5. **`unknown` is always representable** for externally supplied enumerations (convention 7); no model may fail an entire sync because one unrecognized value arrived.
6. **No model is a store of user-authored HTML or executable content.** `DM-1.title`/`notes`, `DM-15.label`, `DM-8.reason` and `DM-24.reason` are text values treated as data on render.

### Open Questions

| Id | Question | Owner of the decision | Why it blocks/affects modelling |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-1 | Should the product support **multiple priority profiles** (e.g. a "work" and a "home" profile, switchable) rather than exactly one active profile? This model enforces one active profile per owner via `DM-6.isActive` and `DM-22.defaultPriorityProfileId`. | USER | Multi-profile changes `DM-6` cardinality, adds a profile-selection concept to F-1's UI, and makes `DM-7.profileId` a user-visible dimension. It cannot be added later without touching saved rankings' meaning. |
| OQ-2 | Should **recurring tasks** be supported? `DM-1.origin` currently has a `recurring` member, but no recurrence-rule entity exists. A recurrence must be modelled explicitly (a rule that *generates* task instances) or the `recurring` member should be removed as unreachable. | USER | Either a new entity plus generation history is required, or the enum member is dead and should be deleted before implementation. Leaving it undefined invites an implementer to invent semantics. |
| OQ-3 | Must a focus session always be **bound to a task**? This model requires it (`DM-10.taskId` is mandatory), so an unbound "just a timer" session is not representable. | USER | If unbound sessions are wanted, `DM-10.taskId` becomes nullable, F-3's entry points widen, and F-4's `tasksCompletedViaFocus` attribution needs a new rule. |
| OQ-4 | Is the **single-active-session rule** product-wide (one per owner across all devices, as modelled) or per device? | USER | Per-device would relax `DM-10` invariant 1, change conflict handling when two devices run timers, and change what "focus time today" means in `DM-13`. |
| OQ-5 | What is the **soft-delete grace period** before a deleted task is purged? No default is assumed here. | USER | Sets the restore window in the UI and the retention row in §12. |
| OQ-6 | How long may `DM-9.rawText` (the user's raw captured line) be retained? | USER | Directly affects data minimisation and what "explain this parse" can show after retention elapses. |
| OQ-7 | Is Progress Analytics ever intended to cover **shared or team** data? This model is strictly single-owner. | USER | Team scope changes every scoped entity's identity and the analytics aggregation unit; retrofitting it is expensive. |
| OQ-8 | Do externally synced items need to be **materialised as tasks** (as modelled in `DM-18`), or should the product show a separate mirrored view that only becomes a task on demand? | USER (with Architect) | Determines whether external items consume `DM-1`'s identity space and whether they appear in the F-1 queue and F-4 metrics by default. |
| OQ-9 | Beyond `DM-24`, is a user-facing **undo history** required (e.g. undo last N actions)? | USER | An undo surface imposes stricter sequencing and retention than an audit log, and would need an explicit operation stack rather than event summaries. |
